## What changed and why

Two real product problems were reported: detection effectiveness felt close to zero,
and players could effectively not move while a probe ran. Both had the same root
cause, found by auditing the whole detection path and by inspecting available client
artifacts and the Paper 1.21.11 server path:

**Everything ran through one interactive mechanism, unattended, on every join.**

The server writes a translatable component onto a temporary sign, opens that sign's
editor on the client, and reads back the text the client submits. The client can only
answer by opening a screen and submitting it, and the server cannot dismiss that
screen. Running that 27 times on join is the movement problem. The same mechanism is
why detection felt weak: a real player who ignores the editor times out, and one who
closes it without the target's text is reported clean or uncertain.

The fix was to declare each probe's transport honestly, stop running interactive
probes unattended, and then go looking for a genuinely non-interactive signal.

## The gameplay-safety fix

Every probe now declares its transport in configuration. It is never inferred from the
probe id.

```yaml
transport: PASSIVE | INTERACTIVE
```

- `PASSIVE` reads an already-available signal. No client UI, no input capture, and
  the only kind allowed to run unattended.
- `INTERACTIVE` needs the client to open and submit UI.

**An absent declaration fails closed to `INTERACTIVE`**, so a newly added probe can
never silently join the automatic path. Admission is enforced in the registry:

```text
automatic-eligible = enabled && automatic && (transport == PASSIVE || auto-check.interactive)
```

No fake fix was applied. There is no movement cancellation, velocity change,
teleport, slowness, freeze, spectator, or movement lock anywhere in the plugin, and
there never was. The problem was hidden by configuration, and configuration was the
correct place to fix it.

## Passive detection

Passive detection was investigated properly before it was built, against available
artifacts rather than assumption. Entries without an artifact remain explicitly
unknown:

| Client | Passive server-bound signal | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vanilla | `minecraft:brand` only | `BrandPayload` in the server jar |
| Clean Fabric | `minecraft:brand` only | Fabric Loader contains no client-to-server networking; **it sends no mod list** |
| Meteor | **none** | no `registerGlobalReceiver`, no send; `PacketUtils` only maps packet class names |
| AppleSkin | **none** | three `registerGlobalReceiver` calls, all server-to-client |
| Jade | **`jade:client_handshake` on join** | `ClientPlayConnectionEvents.JOIN` handler sends it unconditionally |
| Litematica | `servux:litematics` exists, not join-triggered | no join hook in the jar |
| Forwarded, Cezar, Nova | unknown | no build available |

So there is no generic mod list to read, and none was invented. But Jade proved a real
signal exists, and it proved the delivery path is supported.

The full chain, every link verified against the real Jade jar and the real Paper
1.21.11 server jar:

```text
Jade: ClientPlayConnectionEvents.JOIN
  -> ClientPlayNetworking.send(new ClientHandshakePacket("9"))
  -> inbound custom payload on channel "jade:client_handshake"
  -> server has no codec for that channel, so it decodes as DiscardedPayload,
     which preserves the channel id and the raw bytes
  -> ServerCommonPacketListenerImpl.handleCustomPayload
  -> CraftServer.getMessenger().dispatchIncomingMessage(conn, channel, data)
  -> StandardMessenger dispatches to listeners registered for that exact channel
  -> jade-network-handshake probe: STRONG evidence, automatic, zero UI
```

This uses only the supported Bukkit/Paper plugin-messaging API. No NMS, no Netty, no
packet rewriting, no new dependency, and nothing is ever sent to the client, so it
cannot prompt the client to do anything either.

**Its absence proves nothing.** A client that does not send the channel is `CLEAN`, so
this cannot produce a false positive.

**It is `LIVE_VERIFIED`.** On 2026-10-09 a real client and a real server were both
available, and the passive path was exercised end to end.

```text
server: Paper 1.21.11, Java 21.0.12.1, 127.0.0.1:25599, this plugin installed
client: Fabric Loader 0.19.5, Minecraft 1.21.11, offline mode
mods:   fabric-api 0.141.6+1.21.11 + Jade 21.1.6+fabric   (real jar)

passiveObserver=READY channels=[jade:client_handshake]
AutoCheck SCHEDULED player=... automaticProbes=1
AutoCheck VERDICT player=... verdict=BLOCKED diagnosticStatus=DETECTED
             reason=passive scan complete: authoritative exact identity for 1
             probe(s) mods=Jade (network handshake)
AutoCheck ENFORCEMENT player=... action=NONE reason=result is not confirmed
```

A second run used the same player UUID and the same launcher with an empty mods
directory, and reported `verdict=CLEAN ... mods=none`. The verdict therefore follows
the mod rather than the account, which is the property a false positive would break.

The 41 interactive probes were not driven in this session and remain `UNVERIFIED`.

## Passive identity does not enforce

`client-detection.passive.enforce` is `false`.

A confirmed passive detection is reported in `/vac detections` and `/vac status`, but
does not reach enforcement. The only channel proven so far belongs to Jade, a
legitimate utility mod, so kicking players for it automatically would be a false
positive - exactly the class of problem this release exists to remove. The live
session confirmed this: a real player with Jade installed received
`action=NONE reason=result is not confirmed`.

Operators who want passive identity actionable can set the flag, and should understand
that it will then kick Jade users.

## Detection coverage

```text
42 probe definitions
0   VERIFIED / 1 LIVE_VERIFIED   jade-network-handshake, session 2026-10-09
41  UNVERIFIED
18  DISABLED     intentionally not executed, with a recorded reason
1   PASSIVE      declared inbound channel, no client UI
41  INTERACTIVE  answered through the sign editor
24  enabled and manual-eligible
17  automatic-policy entries; 1 eligible by default, 17 with auto-check.interactive: true
3   DETECTED-capable in the catalog; 1 is automatic by default
```

One probe is backed by a recorded live client session. Artifact inspection and
bytecode analysis are recorded as evidence for the rest, but neither substitutes
for a live client session, so those 41 remain `UNVERIFIED`.

**What percentage of the catalog is detectable automatically without opening a client
UI? 1 of 42, about 2.4%.** That number is not optimized. Most client mods transmit
nothing about themselves, and the ones that do are legitimate utilities.

Artifact-backed but live-unverified definitions include:

| Probe | Version | Observable evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `meteor-client` | Meteor Client 1.21.11-86 | key exists in the inspected artifact; client response unobserved |
| `apple-skin` | AppleSkin 3.0.8 | key exists in the inspected artifact; client response unobserved |
| `jade-network-handshake` | Jade 21.1.6 | passive sender/receiver path established from artifacts; client session unobserved |

These are artifact or code-path observations, not live validation. A newer build of
the same mod is not covered by that evidence.

Eighteen probes are disabled, each with a recorded reason. Fourteen are keybind
probes with no authoritative identity route; the remaining four are:

| Probe | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| `itemscroller` | identifier matches a fabricated template with no confirmable artifact |
| `cezar-client` | requested, but no build available to confirm an identifier |
| `nova-client` | requested, but no build available to confirm an identifier |
| `forwarded` | requested, but no build available to confirm an identifier |

The three requested clients use a visibly marked placeholder key. They are disabled on
purpose: a placeholder key resolves to nothing on a real client, so an enabled probe
would report `CLEAN` forever and give false assurance that the client was being
checked.

## What a scan can conclude

| Conclusion | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `DETECTED` | Exact structured identity, an exact configured response, or a client resolved a key only the target defines |
| `CLEAN` | The client answered and nothing indicated a probed target |
| `UNCERTAIN` | The client rendered translated text with no identity attached |
| `PROTECTED` | The response channel was neutralized |
| `TIMEOUT` | No answer inside the deadline; never clean, never detected |
| `UNSUPPORTED` | The transport cannot carry this probe |
| `ERROR` | Transport, scheduling, or processing failure; never a detection |
| `SKIPPED` | Policy or eligibility stop |

Scans no longer add detections up numerically. A detection requires authoritative
evidence for a specific probe. Multiple weak signals are reported `UNCERTAIN` together
with the reason they were not promoted, and a `DETECTED` that arrives without
authoritative evidence is refused defensively.

## Locale-independent detection

A probe that declares `identity-resolution: true` accepts **any** non-sentinel
resolution of its own target-specific key, not only the recorded default-locale
string.

The evaluator supports locale-independent identity when a probe has justified
`identity-resolution: true`. The current catalog does not promote any probe to
that state without live evidence. The sentinel check still guarantees a client
without the key is never detected.

## What is never evidence

None of these can produce a detection, by design and by test:

- substring, prefix, or partial matches
- generic visible text or arbitrary localized text
- a guessed or merely plausible mod identifier, including the disabled placeholders
- client brand, including Fabric brand - a Fabric client running Meteor and one
  running only Sodium present the same brand
- timing, latency, or absence of a response
- a probe id or category that merely looks right
- a channel name that is merely similar to a declared one

`/vac probe <id>` shows, per probe, the evidence quality, the observable artifact, the
expected clean and target behaviour, and whether the probe can reach `DETECTED` at all.

## Breaking changes

1. **Interactive probes no longer run automatically.** With the default
   `auto-check.interactive: false`, an automatic join scan opens no client UI and
   mutates no world. Use `/vac check <player>` for interactive verification.
2. **`transport` is required metadata** and defaults to `INTERACTIVE`.
3. **A resolved-but-unmatched response is now `UNCERTAIN`, not `CLEAN`.**
4. **A `PASSIVE` probe may not declare `expected-response` or `identity-resolution`**,
   and an `INTERACTIVE` probe may not declare a `passive-channel`.
5. **`VERIFIED` requires evidence metadata** on any probe, including passive ones.
6. **Passive-only detections do not enforce** unless `passive.enforce: true`.

### Migration

- The legacy `auto-check.probes` list syntax is still parsed into per-probe
  `automatic` policy. It cannot bypass the transport gate.
- Existing `manual`, `automatic`, `verification`, `category`, `source`, `notes`, and
  `expected-response` fields are preserved as authored.
- New keys default safely when absent: `transport` to `INTERACTIVE`,
  `identity-resolution` to `false`, `passive.enforce` to `false`.
- Reload is pre-validated; a rejected configuration leaves the last known-good
  registry active.
- **If you want the old unattended behaviour back**, set
  `client-detection.auto-check.interactive: true`, after reading the caveat in
  `client-detection.yml`. It will repeatedly open a sign editor on joining players and
  block their movement while it waits.

## Configuration reference

New keys in `client-detection.yml`:

```yaml
client-detection:
  passive:
    enforce: false        # may a passive-only detection reach enforcement
  auto-check:
    interactive: false    # may INTERACTIVE probes run unattended (captures player input)
  probes:
    <id>:
      transport: PASSIVE | INTERACTIVE   # required; defaults to INTERACTIVE
      passive-channel: "mod:channel"      # required for PASSIVE, rejected for INTERACTIVE
      identity-resolution: true           # key is defined only by this target
```

`/vac status` reports `Probes passive/interactive`, `Automatic-eligible`,
`Blocked-by-transport`, passive observer state, and per-channel observation counts.
`/vac status verbose` adds the eligibility breakdown, evidence strengths, and the
conclusion reason for every scan. No raw payloads are shown or stored.

## Commands and permissions

Unchanged in 0.2.1, and now the primary way to run interactive detection:

| Command | Permission | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/vac check <player>` | `vanticheat.probe` | manual interactive scan |
| `/vac check <player> <probe-ids>` | `vanticheat.probe` | manual scan of specific probes |
| `/vacprobe <player>` | `vanticheat.probe` | configured manual probes |
| `/vac status [verbose]` | `vanticheat.status` | runtime health and coverage |
| `/vac probes` | `vanticheat.admin` | catalog with per-probe status |
| `/vac probe <probe-id>` | `vanticheat.admin` | full validity row for one probe |
| `/vac detections` | `vanticheat.status` | recent confirmed detections |
| `/vac reload` | `vanticheat.reload` | pre-validated atomic reload |
| `/vac lunar <player>` | `vanticheat.admin` | Lunar/Apollo policy state |
| `/vac trust add\|remove\|list` | `vanticheat.admin` | trusted-player management |

## Client probe health

Separate from detection, and never a detection: `READY`, `RESPONSIVE`, `UNSUPPORTED`,
`UNRESPONSIVE`, `TIMED_OUT`, `INTERRUPTED`. This is transport and client readiness
only. It says nothing about a player's hardware, and `ClientProbeHealth` exposes a
`detectionSignal()` that is `false` for every value, asserted by test.

## Security posture

```text
gameplay-freeze mechanisms              0
direct scheduler use            only PaperFoliaScheduler
NMS/Netty access added          1 path     NmsSignPackets, interactive transport only
unsolicited payloads sent to a client   0
raw payload retention or logging        0
network I/O                             0
embedded secrets                        0
path traversal                          0
```

Optional integrations (Apollo, Floodgate, Geyser) are `softdepend` and resolved
through the plugin manager; absence degrades to a documented state.

### The one NMS dependency, stated plainly

`NmsSignPackets` reaches server internals through reflection: `net.minecraft.core.BlockPos`,
`net.minecraft.network.protocol.game.ClientboundBlockEntityDataPacket`,
`ClientboundOpenSignEditorPacket`, and `ServerPlayer.connection`. It exists only to open the sign
editor for the INTERACTIVE transport. Earlier revisions of these notes claimed zero NMS access;
that was wrong for the interactive path, and the claim is corrected here.

Consequences an operator should know:

- The **passive** path is pure public API and carries no NMS dependency. If these internals ever
  move on a server update, the passive Jade detection and every non-interactive safety property
  keep working; only the interactive sign round trip is affected.
- Every reflective lookup is guarded and degrades to a transport error, which is reported as
  `ERROR` and can never become a detection. A server update cannot turn this into a false
  positive, but it can silently stop interactive detection, which would show up as
  `diagnostic=ERROR` or `noResponse` rather than as a wrong verdict.

See [`testing/DETECTION-AND-ENFORCEMENT.md`](testing/DETECTION-AND-ENFORCEMENT.md).

## Validation

```text
artifact  vanticheat-0.2.1.jar
size      413378 bytes
sha256    a0b4d20b750c1faf829f512ee5a1f91079fec7bf1cec9e5a794876f6f9acf5b3

948 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped
mvn -q clean verify successful
production JAR contains plugin.yml and no test/source/proxy classes
git diff --check clean
```

The SHA-256 above is now stable across rebuilds. `pom.xml` sets
`project.build.outputTimestamp`, so two clean builds of this tree produce a
byte-identical jar; this was verified by building twice and comparing digests.
Before that property was set, the jar embedded wall-clock entry timestamps and
every rebuild produced a different digest for identical content, which made
"verify the shipped artifact" impossible to state honestly. Bump the property when
cutting a new release.

Coverage includes Bedrock zero-probe, `UNKNOWN` fail-closed, every result status, the
lifecycle and exactly-once invariants, the P31.1 cleanup-target behavior, the
transport gate, passive evidence binding and rejection, reconnect and disconnect
isolation, memory bounds, brand-is-context-only, and fourteen false-positive attack
cases.

## Known limitations

- **Automatic coverage is 1 of 42 probes.** Interactive verification is the only route
  for the rest.
- **The shipped catalog detects no cheat client.** The interactive transport is proven working
  and a real Meteor Client is visible through it, but `meteor-client` deliberately declares no
  expected response: it returned exactly "Open GUI", which is ordinary English UI text, and a
  false positive on a `client`-category probe means kicking a legitimate player. Vanilla
  Minecraft and all 55 mods in the test workspace define no other source of that string, but
  that is evidence about this environment, not proof. See
  [`testing/DETECTION-AND-ENFORCEMENT.md`](testing/DETECTION-AND-ENFORCEMENT.md).
- **No server-authoritative behavioural detection exists.** Every probe is mod-identity based.
  There is no reach, timing, rotation, movement or flight detector, so a client that runs no
  recognisable mod is never challenged on behaviour.
- **The interactive transport depends on NMS internals.** See the note above. The passive path
  does not.
- `jade-network-handshake` is `LIVE_VERIFIED` as of 2026-10-09, but only on Paper. It was
  not exercised on Folia, and a passive channel that works on Paper is not automatically
  correct on Folia.
- Passive signals are client-asserted; a modified client can suppress them. A player who
  simply removes Jade produces no signal at all, which reads as `CLEAN`.
- The three requested clients are disabled with placeholder keys.
- Xaero Minimap and Xaero World Map remain diagnostic-only legitimate identities;
  neither is an enforcement target.
- Server-observable movement and combat behavior detection is still not part of the
  product, and this release did not add any.
- Bedrock isolation, the Apollo integration, and all 41 interactive probe responses
  were not validated live in this release.

```

`docs/RELEASE-NOTES-1.0.0.md`:

```md
# VAntiCheat 1.0.0

First stable release. The detection contract is now frozen.

Paper and Folia 1.21.11, Java 21.

## What 1.0.0 means

1.0.0 is a stability commitment about **behaviour and configuration**, not a claim
of complete cheat detection. From this release:

- The probe result vocabulary (`CLEAN`, `DETECTED`, `UNCERTAIN`, `PROTECTED`,
  `TIMEOUT`, `UNSUPPORTED`, `ERROR`, `SKIPPED`) is frozen. A semantic change to any
  of these requires a major version.
- The `transport` gate is frozen. `automatic-eligible = enabled && automatic &&
  (transport == PASSIVE || auto-check.interactive)`.
- Existing configuration keys keep working. New keys default to the conservative
  value, never to a newly-permissive one.
- The safety properties below are contractual. Removing one is a breaking change,
  not a patch.

It is **not** a claim that VAntiCheat detects cheat clients. With the shipped
catalog, no probe can reach enforcement. That is stated plainly below, and it is
the most important thing to read before deploying.

## Read this before deploying

**The shipped catalog punishes nobody.** Of 42 probe definitions, 3 can reach
`DETECTED`, and all 3 are legitimate identities:

| Probe | Result | Enforcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jade-network-handshake` | `DETECTED` on join | `passive.enforce: false`, so no kick |
| `xaeros-minimap` | `DETECTED` via `/vac check` | legitimate utility, never a target |
| `xaeros-worldmap` | `DETECTED` via `/vac check` | legitimate utility, never a target |

Every other probe is either `UNCERTAIN` at best or reports the client as `CLEAN`.
Enforcement exists, is tested, and is reachable, but nothing in the default
catalog currently triggers it. If you enable `passive.enforce: true`, you are
choosing to kick Jade users. That is a real false positive, and the live session
recorded it as `action=NONE reason=result is not confirmed`.

## What changed since 0.2.1

Behaviour is unchanged. This release is the 0.2.1 codebase, with the version
promoted and the stability contract written down. The substantive work in
0.2.1 (the `transport` gate, passive detection, the `UNCERTAIN` correction,
health reporting, the protection layer, brand caching, and the coverage matrix)
is documented in [`RELEASE-NOTES-0.2.1.md`](RELEASE-NOTES-0.2.1.md) and is not
repeated here.

What is new in 1.0.0:

- Version `1.0.0` in `pom.xml` and therefore in `plugin.yml`, via `${project.version}`.
- This document, and the frozen-contract statement above.
- A corrected coverage claim in the README. It previously said "1 LIVE_VERIFIED"
  and "41 UNVERIFIED" while also stating three probes were live-verified
  elsewhere in the same file. The enforced truth is 3 `LIVE_VERIFIED` and 39
  `UNVERIFIED`, and `ClientCoverageMatrixTest.theHonestyCorrectionIsPreserved`
  asserts exactly those three probe ids. The stale text was a documentation
  defect, not a code defect.

There are no code changes between 0.2.1 and 1.0.0.

## Upgrade notes

No migration is required. Configuration written for 0.2.1 loads unchanged.

- `plugin.yml` reports `version: 1.0.0` automatically; there is no version
  constant to edit by hand.
- `auto-check.probes` (the legacy list form) is still accepted as a migration
  format, and still cannot bypass the transport gate.
- Invalid client-detection configuration leaves the last known-good registry
  active. It never partially applies.
- `/vac reload` remains rejected when client detection was unavailable at
  startup. Fix the config and restart the plugin.

## Detection coverage, as enforced

```text
42 probe definitions
0   VERIFIED          still unused: this project promotes only on a live session
3   LIVE_VERIFIED     jade-network-handshake, xaeros-minimap, xaeros-worldmap
39  UNVERIFIED
18  DISABLED          each with a recorded reason
1   PASSIVE           declared inbound channel, no client UI
41  INTERACTIVE       sign-editor transport
24  enabled and manual-eligible
17  automatic-policy entries; 1 eligible by default, 17 with auto-check.interactive: true
3   DETECTED-capable in the catalog; 1 is automatic by default
```

**Automatic coverage without opening a client UI is 1 of 42, about 2.4%.**
This is a deliberate ceiling, not an oversight. Fabric Loader sends no mod list,
Meteor registers no server-bound channel at all, and the only proven passive
signal belongs to a legitimate utility mod. See `README.md` for the full Jade
chain.

## Safety properties, now contractual

```text
gameplay-freeze mechanisms (velocity, teleport, slowness, freeze, spectator, lock)  0
automatic path that opens client UI with shipped defaults                                0
world mutation on an automatic join scan                                                0
raw payload retention or logging                                                        0
unsolicited payloads sent to a client                                                    0
Bedrock players receiving probes                                                        0
legitimate mods as enforcement targets                                                  0
TIMEOUT / UNSUPPORTED / CLEAN / ERROR reaching enforcement                               0
```

These are asserted by deterministic tests and static audit, not by live player
measurement. That distinction is part of the contract: the claims are about code
paths and simulated sessions.

The one NMS dependency, `NmsSignPackets`, exists only to open the sign editor for
the interactive transport. Every reflective lookup is guarded and degrades to
`ERROR`, which can never become a detection. A server update can therefore stop
interactive detection, but cannot turn it into a false positive. The passive path
is pure public API and does not depend on it.

## Validation

```text
artifact  vanticheat-1.0.0.jar
size      413377 bytes
sha256    00f31135a01fffc5418e8292c8334e0987ed1e0741d48e5cf6c424d62f90aea0

948 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped

```

The build is byte-reproducible: `pom.xml` pins `project.build.outputTimestamp` to
the release date, so two clean builds of this tree produce an identical jar. This
was verified by building twice and comparing digests. `pom.xml` deliberately does
**not** enable resource filtering, so the digest does not depend on the local
Maven or JDK paths.

To verify the artifact you actually downloaded:

```bash
sha256sum VAntiCheat-1.0.0.jar
```

Note that the jar name produced by `mvn package` is
`vanticheat-1.0.0.jar` (the artifact id). Servers only require that it be dropped
into `plugins/`; the filename does not matter.

## Known limitations

These are the honest gaps at 1.0.0:

- **No probe in the shipped catalog can kick anyone.** See above.
- **No server-authoritative behavioural detection exists.** There is no reach,
  timing, rotation, movement, or flight detector. A client running no
  recognisable mod is never challenged on behaviour. This is the single largest
  gap, and it is a design decision rather than a missing feature: the movement and
  combat detectors from the legacy 1.3.x product were deliberately removed rather
  than carried forward without the evidence to support them.
- **Automatic coverage is 1 of 42 probes.** The rest need `/vac check`.
- **The interactive transport depends on NMS internals.** Verified on Paper
  1.21.11 only.
- **`jade-network-handshake` is `LIVE_VERIFIED` on Paper, not on Folia.** A passive
  channel that works on Paper is not automatically correct on Folia.
- **Passive signals are client-asserted.** A player who removes Jade produces no
  signal, which reads as `CLEAN`.
- **39 probes are `UNVERIFIED`.** Their evidence is artifact inspection, bytecode
  inspection, and deterministic stubs. A newer build of the same mod is not
  covered by that evidence.
- Bedrock isolation, the Apollo/Lunar integration, and trusted-player enforcement
  were not validated live in this release.

## What would be a breaking change

Per semantic versioning, these require a 2.0.0:

- Changing the meaning of any result status.
- Making a probe automatic-eligible without an explicit operator opt-in.
- Enabling enforcement for a legitimate-mod identity by default.
- Removing or weakening any safety property listed above.
- Requiring a new configuration key that does not have a conservative default.
```

`docs/TRUSTED-PLAYERS.md`:

```md
# Trusted Players

## Commands

Administrators with `vanticheat.admin` may use:

```text
/vac help
/vac reload
/vac trust PlayerName
/vac trust add PlayerName
/vac trust remove PlayerName
/vac trust list
```

Console is always authorized. In-game players require the dedicated permission; ordinary players cannot modify the list. The command provides online-player completion and trusted-name completion for removal.

`/vac reload` is also restricted to `vanticheat.admin` for in-game users. It
reinitializes VAntiCheat and applies configuration changes without invoking
Bukkit's global `/reload` command.

## Persistence and identity

Trusted players are stored in `plugins/VAntiCheat/data/trusted-players.yml`. UUID is authoritative, while the current name is retained for readable listings. Known offline players can be trusted through the server's cached offline-player lookup; no network lookup occurs from the command or enforcement path. Entries survive restart and are written with an atomic temporary-file replacement where supported.

## Enforcement policy

The trusted check is centralized in `EnforcementService`. Every current enforcement caller, including manual client probes and automatic join checks, still performs detection and produces evidence. If the target UUID is trusted, the enforcement decision is changed to `NONE` and the executor is not called. The result remains detected/confirmed rather than being relabeled clean.

Removing trust updates the in-memory set immediately, so subsequent enforcement follows the normal policy without restart. Trusted status is not invisibility; it means only that VAntiCheat does not punish the player.

```

`docs/archive-1.3.x/ANTI-FREECAM.md`:

```md
# Anti-Freecam

Behavior-based camera/body divergence detection plus server-authoritative
exposure prevention. No client fingerprinting: renamed, modified, or
timing-altered Freecam clients are caught by what they *do*, not what they
*claim to be*.

## Architecture

```
PacketEvents (inbound movement/rotation, outbound world data)
  → AntiFreecamPackets      (normalize only: zero Bukkit, fail-open)
  → Player State            (BodySnapshot region-written / Netty-read)
  → DivergenceAnalyzer      (rotation-without-movement, pure logic)
  → Sightline               (region-thread raycast + reach validation)
  → ExposureGuard           (depth shadow + distance gate on outbound)
  → Evidence                (violations → confidence → evidence → punishment)
```

Components (`com.hexa.vanticheat.antifreecam`):

| Class | Role | Thread |
|---|---|---|
| `AntiFreecamManager` | Facade: body truth, validation, evidence, lifecycle | region |
| `AntiFreecamPackets` | Single PacketEvents listener (in + out) | Netty |
| `BodySnapshot` / `CameraObservation` | Immutable body / mutable observation | both (lock-free) |
| `DivergenceAnalyzer` | Multi-signal scoring, no Bukkit | any |
| `Sightline` | Bounded raycast + reach check | region only |
| `ExposureGuard` | Outbound information withholding | Netty |
| `AntiFreecamConfig` | Small flat snapshot of `anti-freecam:` | load-time |

## Prevention model (exposure-based, learned from a live regression)

FPAntiFreeCam hides everything below a static `voidY`. The first version of
this system hid tile entities below a body-relative plane — and live QA
proved that wrong: stripped tile data never healed (updates were suppressed
too), producing "invisible until touched" chests. Body-distance proxies for
*world data* are therefore gone. The corrected rule:

- **World data is server-authorized.** Chunk loading is body-driven, so every
  emitted chunk/block/tile-entity/signal packet is already part of the body's
  legitimate world state. The guard never withholds it (except opt-in
  `shadow-chunks` paranoia mode, which trades movement integrity for hiding).
- **Entities are gated** (no rendering coupling — hiding an entity cannot
  create holes or invisible walls):
  - below the depth shadow (`prevention.depth-margin`, default 10): spawns,
    metadata, entity-bound sounds withheld;
  - beyond the distance gate (`prevention.distance-limit`, default 64):
    non-player spawns withheld, blinding ESP/radar through a detached camera.
- **Player entities are never suppressed** (legitimate long-distance
  rendering must keep working; player ESP is Anti-ESP's job).

Deliberately NOT ported from FPAntiFreeCam: the anvil translation-key probe
(client-signature detection — bypassed by renaming the mod) and the static
floor (breaks none of our cases but is less precise than body-relative).

## Detection model

Independent signals, evidence only when `detection.min-signals` (default 2)
corroborate:

- `ROTATION_WITHOUT_MOVEMENT` — sustained look change with no position change
  inside `rotate-window-ms` (detached camera). Position packets reset it, so
  walking/elytra/PvP never accumulate.
- `REACH_VIOLATION` — interaction target beyond `interact-reach` from the
  body eye. Blatant cases (`reach + 3`) or corroborated cases are cancelled.
- `SIGHTLINE_VIOLATION` — target in reach but occluded (bounded raycast).
  Recorded, never used to cancel (avoids wall-edge false positives).

Exemptions (no duplicate system — uses `VConfig.exempt`, gamemode/vehicle
state, and grace timestamps): spectator, vehicle, teleport/respawn/death/
world-change grace (3 s), ops/bypass permission.

## Configuration (`anti-freecam:`)

See `config.yml`. Small on purpose: `enabled`, `prevention.*`,
`detection.*`, `evidence-weight`, `debug`, `performance.*`. Migration v5
carries the old `freecam.enabled` master switch forward; all other old keys
are ignored.

## Operations

- `/vac status` — module row; `/vac diagnostics` — guard counters
  (`evaluated/suppressed/shadowedBlocks/tracked`).
- `/vac debug freecam <player>` — body truth, packet observation, look
  accumulation, signals, confidence. Rate-limited by design (on demand).
- `anti-freecam.debug: true` — throttled suppression trace to console.

## Camera forcing: tested, ineffective, not shipped

Live QA (isolated harness, real Freecam client): a single server Camera
packet, repeated spam (5 and 20 sends), and re-detach attempts all produced
zero visible effect — the mod reasserts its local camera every client tick
and ignores the packet completely (result C). Vanilla clients are unaffected
by the packet (no flicker). Conclusion: no server packet can force a
client-local camera; no camera lock is implemented, and none is claimed.
The active consequence path is persistence-gated evidence → the existing
punishment pipeline (kick per `forbidden_mod` policy).

## Detection: persistence-gated consequence

A lone look-sweep never triggers evidence (min-signals rule). Sustained
across `detection.persistence-windows` consecutive evaluations (~5s each,
default 6 ≈ 30s of frozen body + 180°+ sweeps) it becomes its own
corroboration and emits evidence. Legitimate play cannot hold that pattern:
walking/elytra/PvP move the body (resets accumulation), teleports and grace
reset the streak, spectator/vehicle/exempt skip evaluation.

## Known limitation (protocol, not a bug)

The server cannot unsend terrain the client already holds around the body,
and it must not break legitimate chunk rendering. Prevention withholds
*entity* information outside body context (deep/distant spawns, metadata,
entity sounds); chest *boxes* and terrain inside body-loaded chunks still
render at a detached camera, because that data is body-authorized —
withholding it would break vanilla for legitimate players (proven live).
Detection (camera-sweep signals) + interaction cancellation cover what
prevention structurally cannot: the camera may look, but out-of-reach use is
blocked and evidenced.

```

```md
# VAntiCheat configuration reference

All keys live in `plugins/VAntiCheat/config.yml`. Unknown keys are ignored;
invalid values fall back safely with a console warning. Editing any section
by hand means the `security.profile` preset is customized (shown as your
chosen base profile everywhere).

## security.profile — presets

| Preset | Detection aggression | Punishment | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lenient` | ×0.7 weights, +15 confidence gate | Cautious | Quiet/private servers |
| `standard` | ×1.0, no gate shift | Balanced | Most servers (start here) |
| `hardcore` | ×1.25, −5 gate | Firm on strong evidence | Aggressive SMP |
| `paranoid` | ×1.1, max collection | Proof-gated, never reckless | Investigation servers |

```yaml
# Normal server
security: { profile: standard }
# Aggressive SMP
security: { profile: hardcore }
# Maximum investigation
security: { profile: paranoid }
```

## Section map

- `general` — master switch, debug logging, op exemption
- `features` — edition gates (core, client-security, behavior, anti-xray,
  anti-esp, advanced-simulation); disable whole modules here
- `client_security` / `modlist` / `antispoof` — brand/channel identification
- `antixray` — sample size, valuable blocks, statistical thresholds
- `anti_esp` — rolling correlation window (`history_seconds`), minimap policy
- `behavior` — per-check toggles, reach limit, violation decay
- `confidence` — signal weights + per-class idle decay (weak/medium/strong)
- `punishment` + `punishments` — global gates + per-category actions
  (`none|alert|warn|kick|tempban|ban`); bans need `minimum-independent-signals`
- `trust.bypass` — per-category staff bypass (no global bypass exists)
- `evidence` / `storage` — history toggle, retention days, file-size rotation
- `performance` — memory bounds; `profiling` enables sampled timings
- `alerts` — staff alerts toggle + silence threshold (`min-confidence`)
- `qa.punishment.dry-run` — log instead of kick/ban (testing only)
- `clients` / `mods` — per-client/mod enable + action overrides

## Messages

`plugins/VAntiCheat/messages.yml` categories: `general`, `commands`,
`status`, `inspect`, `alerts`, `diagnostics`, `client-security`,
`punishment`, `errors`. Placeholders: `%player% %uuid% %ping% %check%
%confidence% %vl% %action% %client% %mod% %profile% %platform%
%server_version%` (`{name}` also works). Colors: `&0-9a-f`, `&l` bold,
`&o` italic, `&n` underline, `&r` reset. Templates are parsed once per
reload; placeholder values can never inject colors. Missing keys use
built-ins, so old files survive updates.

`docs/testing/CONFIGURATION-VALIDATION.md`:

```md
# Configuration Validation

Generated by the exhaustive configuration campaign. Every option listed here was discovered by
reading the shipped resources and the production parsers, then exercised through
`ConfigurationContractTest`, `ClientDetectionConfigTest`, `ShippedConfigurationTest`,
`ProbeTransportConfigTest`, `InventoryGuardTest`, and the pre-existing configuration tests.

Status labels: `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED_NOT_AVAILABLE`, `NOT_APPLICABLE`, `NOT_TESTED`.

## Inventory summary

| File | Leaf keys | Parser | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `client-detection.yml` | 486 total, of which **43** are scalar options and 443 are per-probe fields | `ClientDetectionConfig`, `SecurityLimits` | Hand-rolled line parser, no YAML library |
| `config.yml` | **8** | `ConfigurationLoader`, `EnforcementConfig`, `LunarPolicyConfig` | Three independent line parsers read the same file |
| `messages.yml` | **54** | `Messages` | Every key is a message template |
| `plugin.yml` | command/permission metadata | Bukkit | `api-version: '1.21'` |

The 43 scalar `client-detection.yml` options are the 9 top-level scalars, 1 `passive.enforce`,
5 `auto-check.*`, and 16 `protection.*`; the remaining 443 are the 42 probe definitions.

`config.yml` is read by **three** parsers that each walk the file independently. That is a real
structural hazard and is tested explicitly below.

## `config.yml` — 8 keys, all covered

| Key | Type | Default | Tested values | Runtime effect verified | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vanticheat.enabled` | boolean | `true` | `true`, `false`, missing file, `yes`/`1`/`on`/empty (invalid) | yes — `FoundationConfig.enabled()`; adopted for both boolean values; invalid falls back to default rather than throwing | PASS |
| `vanticheat.debug` | boolean | `false` | `true`, `false` | yes — adopted in both states | PASS |
| `detection.enabled` | boolean | `true` | `true`, `false` | yes — `detectionEnabled()`; verified it does **not** disturb `vanticheat.*` or `enforcement.*` | PASS |
| `enforcement.enabled` | boolean | `true` | `true`, `false` | yes — feeds `DefaultEnforcementPolicy`; `false` yields `action=NONE` | PASS |
| `enforcement.confirmed-detection.message` | string | `Cheating detected.` | quoted, unquoted, blank, whitespace-only | yes — blank is rejected by the record constructor, and the loader then disables enforcement rather than running with an unusable message | PASS |
| `lunar.enabled` | boolean | `true` | `true`, `false` | yes — `LunarPolicyConfig.enabled()` | PASS |
| `lunar.minimap.enabled` | boolean | `true` | `true`, `false` | yes — `minimapEnabled()` | PASS |
| `lunar.minimap.action` | enum | `DISABLE` | `DISABLE`, `BAN` (unsupported) | yes — any value other than `DISABLE` throws and disables the whole lunar policy, so the operator never gets a silently-ignored setting | PASS |

**No dead keys.** Every one of the 8 `config.yml` keys is read by a parser and its effect is
asserted. `lunar.minimap.action` is the only key that accepts exactly one value; that is
intentional and documented in the shipped file.

### Isolation requirement

The campaign explicitly tested that one invalid key cannot corrupt unrelated settings:

- A non-boolean `vanticheat.enabled` falls back to defaults without discarding `debug`.
- A non-boolean `detection.enabled` falls back without discarding `vanticheat.*` or `enforcement.*`.
- An unsupported `lunar.minimap.action` disables only the lunar policy.
- A blank enforcement message disables enforcement but preserves the configured string.

Status: **PASS**. One earlier suspicion was investigated and disproved: `ConfigurationLoader.parse`
parses every value under `vanticheat:`/`detection:` as a boolean *before* checking the key name, so an
unknown non-boolean key in those two sections would abort the file. A test
(`unknownKeyUnderDetectionDoesNotAbortTheFile`) was written to prove this and it **passed**,
because `ConfigurationLoader.load` catches the exception and falls back to defaults — which
discards `vanticheat.enabled` and `debug` together with it. The settings are *individually* isolated
only in the sense that the fallback is uniform. A future non-boolean key added under `detection:`
would therefore silently reset `vanticheat.debug`. **Recorded as a low-severity latent fragility,
not fixed, because changing it would alter documented fallback behaviour.**

## `client-detection.yml` scalar options — 25 keys

| Key | Type | Default | Boundary/robustness tested | Runtime effect | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | both values | gates every scan | PASS |
| `double-check` | boolean | `true` | both values | gates the CONFIRMATION pass | PASS |
| `timeout-ticks` | long | `40` | 1, 40, 100000 | passed to `ProbeRequest` | PASS |
| `short-timeout-ticks` | long | `10` | `>= timeout` disables backoff | selects silent-client deadline | PASS |
| `short-timeout-after-consecutive-timeouts` | long | `2` | 1, 2, large | streak threshold | PASS |
| `between-probe-ticks` | long | `0` | 0, positive | delay between batches | PASS |
| `exploit-preventer-line` | boolean | `true` | both values | whether line 3 carries the preventer key | PASS |
| `passive.enforce` | boolean | `false` | both values | **runtime-verified**: gates whether a passive confirmation pass is recorded at all | PASS |
| `auto-check.on-join` | boolean | `true` | both values | gates `AutomaticClientDetectionListener.onJoin` | PASS |
| `auto-check.delay-ticks` | long | `20` | 0, 1, 20, 100000 | coordinator delay; no value throws | PASS |
| `auto-check.first-join-only` | boolean | `false` | both values | gates repeat scans | PASS |
| `auto-check.max-concurrent` | long | `32` | 1, 32, -1 | coordinator bound; negative does not throw | PASS |
| `auto-check.interactive` | boolean | `false` | both values | **runtime-verified live**: the 16 interactive automatic probes are excluded while false and included when true | PASS |
| `protection.*` (16 keys) | mixed | see `SecurityLimits.DEFAULTS` | `0`, negative, `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, malformed duration, out-of-range duration, valid duration | **runtime-verified**: every hostile value clamps to the documented default; a valid value is adopted rather than always clamped | PASS |

### `protection.*` clamping evidence

`SecurityLimits` clamps each limit independently and cannot be disabled by a hand-edited value:

- `0` and negative → the documented default (fail closed)
- `Integer.MAX_VALUE` for `max-payload-bytes` → capped at 1 MiB
- malformed duration (`not-a-duration`, `5 seconds`, empty) → the documented default
- `0s` / `-1s` duration → the documented default
- valid but out-of-range duration → clamped to the nearest bound
- valid in-range duration (`45s`, `2m`) → adopted

Status: **PASS**. This satisfies the requirement that a protection limit cannot be switched off by
editing its value to zero.

## `messages.yml` — 54 keys

Every key is consumed by `Messages`, which is covered by the pre-existing `MessagesTest` and
`MessagePlaceholderTest`. `Messages.audit()` reports unknown or broken placeholders at startup,
which the live server run exercised: the server started and logged no placeholder audit warning.

Status: **PASS** for presence and placeholder integrity. `NOT_TESTED` for the rendered appearance
of every individual message in a live chat, which was not the subject of this campaign.

## Options deliberately not tested

| Item | Status | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plugin.yml` command aliases and tab completion | NOT_TESTED | Requires an operator console session with a live player; not attempted |
| Apollo / Lunar runtime behaviour | BLOCKED_NOT_AVAILABLE | Apollo is `NOT_PRESENT` on the test server, logged at startup; no Lunar client was available |
| Folia-specific scheduler behaviour | BLOCKED_NOT_AVAILABLE | No Folia server was launched in this campaign; Paper-only results must not be read as Folia results |

## Inventory-guard coverage

`InventoryGuardTest` fails permanently if:

- the catalog probe count, enabled count, passive count, or live-verified count drifts
- an INTERACTIVE probe declares a passive channel
- a passive channel is duplicated or unlisted
- an evidence basis becomes authoritative without being listed in the explicit authoritative set
- a live-verified probe does not cite a live session and its date in the catalog record
- a disabled probe becomes manual- or automatic-eligible
- a detected-capable probe is in the `client` category
- a mode declared by the catalog has no evaluator branch, or a declared mode is unused

Verified by fault injection: disabling the live-verified probe made two guards fail, and restoring
the file made them pass.

`docs/testing/DETECTION-AND-ENFORCEMENT.md`:

```md
# Detection and Enforcement

Phase II: proving real cheat detection. Every claim here is backed by a real client session on a
disposable server, and the environment is recorded so each result can be reproduced or dismissed.

Status labels: `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED_NOT_AVAILABLE`, `NOT_APPLICABLE`, `NOT_TESTED`.
UNIT, INTEGRATION and LIVE results are kept separate throughout.

## Environment

| Component | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Server | Paper `1.21.11`, disposable instance in `/tmp/opencode/p2`, `nogui` |
| JVM | OpenJDK **21.0.12.1** |
| Port | `25601`, console driven over RCON (`127.0.0.1:25605`) |
| Client | Minecraft **1.21.11**, **Fabric Loader 0.19.5** |
| Debug mode | `vanticheat.debug: true` for the whole phase, so the transport timeline was captured |
| Plugin artifact | `target/vanticheat-0.2.1.jar` |

Mods used, all real jars from `~/.minecraft/mods`: Jade `21.1.6+fabric`, Xaero's Minimap `26.5.0`,
Xaero's World Map `1.46.0`, AppleSkin `3.0.8`, Meteor Client `1.21.11-86`, Fabric API `0.141.6+1.21.11`.

No production server was used. The live servers are disposable `/tmp` instances. No user data,
credentials or worlds were touched.

## Workstream 1 — The interactive transport works

### Status: PASS (and it corrects a Phase I error)

Phase I reported that the interactive transport "never gets a response from any real client",
based on `noResponse=23` from a `/vac check` against a 24-probe batch. **That conclusion was
wrong.** The transport is confirmed working end to end.

Observed timeline for a single-probe check, from the plugin's own debug timeline:

```text
TRANSPORT_SEND            elapsedMs=4    timeoutTicks=40
TRANSPORT_OPERATION_START elapsedMs=0
CANDIDATE_SELECTION_START elapsedMs=17
CANDIDATE_SELECTION_END   elapsedMs=24   candidateCount=9 strategy=first-candidate-fast-path
REGION_PLACEMENT_START    elapsedMs=26   candidate=0 location=-1,-56,9
SIGN_UPDATED              elapsedMs=173
SIGN_PLACED               elapsedMs=174
BLOCK_ENTITY_PREPARED     elapsedMs=188
BLOCK_ENTITY_SENT         elapsedMs=189
OPEN_SIGN_SENT            elapsedMs=192
CLIENT_RESPONSE           elapsedMs=287  outcome=RESPONSE
PROBE_EVALUATION          elapsedMs=313  probe=meteor-client status=CLEAN evidence=NONE
BATCH_COMPLETE            elapsedMs=314  outcome=RESPONSE
CLEANUP_END               elapsedMs=345
```

A real client answers in roughly **95 ms**. The full 24-probe check finished in **830 ms** with
`noResponse=0` and `noTarget=24`:

```text
Client probe detail player=VACVANILLA probes=24 blockedProbes=0 noTarget=24
                     unattributed=0 noResponse=0 unsupported=0 unverifiedProbes=23
```

### Why Phase I saw timeouts

The Phase I batched runs returned `noResponse=23`. The transport reaches the client in ~190 ms and
the client answers in ~95 ms, so the timeout was not a transport failure. The most likely cause is
that those runs were interrupted: the client process was terminated with `pkill` while a check was
in flight, which the transport correctly reports as a terminal outcome. That is **not confirmed**,
so it is recorded as the explanation I could not prove, rather than as fact.

The important part is not the explanation. It is that the current, repeated, debug-instrumented
runs show `noResponse=0` with sub-100 ms responses, and the transport is now positively verified
rather than assumed broken.

### Mechanism, confirmed from observed data

A temporary, debug-gated diagnostic was added to log the raw response, used for this diagnosis, and
then **removed**; the production artifact hash returned to its exact prior value
(`a0b77d9e…`) afterwards, proving the revert was complete.

Observed response for a probe whose mod is installed, and for one whose mod is absent:

```text
identities=[null, null, null, null]
lines=[Open GUI, ⟦NO_LIQUIDBOUNCE⟧, , ص]        <- Meteor installed: key resolved to "Open GUI"

identities=[null, null, null, null]
lines=[⟦NO_METEOR_CLIENT⟧, ⟦NO_LIQUIDBOUNCE⟧, ⟦NO_BLEACHHACK⟧, ص]   <- clean client: sentinels echoed

identities=[null, null, null, null]
lines=[⟦NO_INVENTORY_PROFILES_NEXT_REFILL⟧, ⟦NO_EMI_CONFIG⟧, ⟦NO_BARITONE⟧, ص]
```

Two conclusions follow directly from this data:

1. **Component identity is unavailable for every client.** `identities` was `[null, null, null,
   null]` for a vanilla client *and* for a modded client. A translatable component submitted
   through a sign editor arrives as rendered text, so the `translate:<key>` identity can never be
   recovered. The `identity-resolution` route is therefore structurally dead, and
   **exact-response matching is the only identification mechanism that works.**
2. **A client without the mod echoes its sentinel**, for every probe, which is why absence never
   becomes a false positive.

## Workstream 2 — Meteor Client

### Status: mechanism PROVEN, detection deliberately NOT enabled

### Status of each candidate route

| Route | Supported? | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Passive client-reported identification | **No** | Meteor registers no server-bound channel; the automatic scan reported `CLEAN mods=none` on a real client |
| Active client-response identification | **Yes, proven** | A real client returned exactly `"Open GUI"`, the string its own `en_us.json` defines for `key.meteor-client.open-gui` |
| Server-authoritative behavioural detection | **Not implemented** | The catalog is entirely mod-identity based; no movement or combat detector exists in the codebase |
| Usable detection path today | **No** | The active route works but is deliberately not used; see below |

### The deliberate decision, and why

A real Meteor Client returned `"Open GUI"`. Adding `expected-response: "Open GUI"` would make the
plugin detect and kick it — proven live, see Workstream 3. **The shipped catalog does not do this,
on purpose.**

Reasoning, from evidence rather than preference:

- The response is **ordinary English UI text**. A false positive on a `client`-category probe means
  **kicking a legitimate player**.
- Scope of the uniqueness check: vanilla Minecraft `1.21.11` contains **0** definitions of that
  exact string, and across all **55** mods in the test workspace only Meteor defines it.
- That is evidence about *this environment*. It is **not** proof that no other mod, resource pack,
  or server-translatable plugin defines `gui.open` → "Open GUI". The plugin cannot rule that out.
- The asymmetry decides it. For `xaeros-minimap` the expected responses are `"Minimap"` and
  `"Open World Map"` — distinctive strings, in a non-enforcement `map` category. For Meteor the
  string is generic and the category *is* enforcement-eligible.

So the capability is real and demonstrated, and the risk is recorded rather than taken. The
catalog entry and `/vac probe meteor-client` both state this, including the observed response.

### What would settle it

A distinctive per-target string, or a server-side behavioural detector for a measurable cheat
behaviour. Neither exists today.

### Note on a documentation defect found while auditing

`NmsSignPackets` uses NMS classes through reflection (`net.minecraft.core.BlockPos`,
`ServerPlayer`, `ClientboundOpenSignEditorPacket`, and so on). The README and release notes state
"no NMS access". That claim is **false for the interactive transport** and is corrected in this
phase's documentation. It is the one part of the plugin that depends on internals, which is a
maintenance and version-fragility risk on a server update.

## Workstream 3 — The complete enforcement path

### Status: PASS, demonstrated live end to end

Because the shipped catalog refuses to enable Meteor detection, the positive enforcement case was
produced on the **disposable server's own config copy only**. The shipped source was verified
unchanged at the same moment:

```text
added expected-response: "Open GUI" to /tmp/opencode/p2/plugins/VAntiCheat/client-detection.yml
rg -c 'expected-response: "Open GUI"' /home/shadi/VAntiCheat/src/main/resources/client-detection.yml
0 - shipped source has NO Open GUI
```

### Observed sequence, real Meteor client

```text
PROBE_EVALUATION probe=meteor-client status=DETECTED evidence=STRONG   (INITIAL pass,  elapsedMs=141)
PROBE_EVALUATION probe=meteor-client status=DETECTED evidence=STRONG   (CONFIRMATION, elapsedMs=247)
Client probe verdict player=VACMET3 verdict=BLOCKED action=KICK reason=confirmed detection
      diagnosticStatus=DETECTED
      resultReason=double-check complete: authoritative exact identity for 1 probe(s)
      evidence=3 mods=Meteor Client
[VAntiCheat] Confirmed detection: VACMET3 - Action: KICK - Mods: Meteor Client
VACMET3 left the game
```

And the player was genuinely gone from the server:

```text
rcon list -> There are 0 of a max of 5 players online:
```

Every stage of the required pipeline is present in that evidence:

| Stage | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Actual test behaviour | real Meteor Client 1.21.11-86 client |
| Validated observation | sign placed, editor opened, client submitted `"Open GUI"` |
| Evidence corroboration | two independent passes, both DETECTED/STRONG |
| Confirmed detection verdict | `verdict=BLOCKED diagnosticStatus=DETECTED` |
| Eligibility gate | `category: client`, passed |
| Configured enforcement decision | `reason=confirmed detection` |
| Expected action | `action=KICK`, player removed from the server |

### Required safety properties, each verified

| Property | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A confirmed finding produces exactly the configured action | PASS | `action=KICK`, `0 players online` |
| Legitimate control is not punished | PASS | vanilla client stayed online: `verdict=CLEAN action=NONE`, `1 of a max of 5 players online` |
| Legitimate utility mods cannot trigger punishment | PASS | Xaero run produced `verdict=BLOCKED` with `action=NONE`, because category is `map` |
| Duplicate findings do not duplicate punishment | PASS | `vac check VACV3 meteor-client,meteor-client,meteor-client` collapsed to `probes=1` |
| TIMEOUT / UNSUPPORTED / CLEAN never punish | PASS | every clean run reported `action=NONE reason=result is not confirmed` |
| Unclassified evidence never confirms | PASS | `ProbeBasisFailClosedTest`, plus live `blockedProbes=0` on the vanilla control |
| Confirmation pass is required | PASS | promotion cites `double-check complete`; an INITIAL-only record never confirmed in tests |

### Honest qualification

This is a **real end-to-end enforcement execution**, and it is the first in this project's history.
But it required enabling a detection route the maintainers deliberately declined to ship. So the
result proves the *pipeline* is correct and safe; it does not prove the *shipped configuration*
would punish anyone. With the shipped catalog, no probe can reach `KICK`, because all three
detected-capable probes are in non-enforcement categories.

## Detection versus enforcement, stated precisely

- **Identity detection** (proven live): Jade, Xaero's Minimap, Xaero's World Map.
- **Cheat identification** (proven live, not shipped): Meteor Client, via `"Open GUI"`.
- **Cheat behaviour detection**: does not exist. No movement, reach, timing or flight detector is
  implemented. A mod's presence is not proof that a cheat is active.

## Remaining blockers

| Blocker | Severity | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No server-authoritative behavioural cheat detector | **High** | Not implemented |
| Shipped catalog cannot detect any cheat client | **High** | By deliberate safety decision, recorded |
| `"Open GUI"` uniqueness cannot be proven, only observed | Medium | Would block shipping this route |
| 39 probes never exercised end to end | Medium | Interactive transport now proven, so this is reachable |
| Folia never launched | Medium | BLOCKED_NOT_AVAILABLE |
| Interactive transport depends on NMS internals | Medium | Documentation corrected; a server update could break it |
| Enforcement proven only via a config override | Medium | Pipeline proven; shipped config intentionally punishes nobody |

## Release recommendation

# `BLOCKED — DO NOT SHIP` as an anti-cheat

Phase II moved the position from "the mechanism is unproven" to "the mechanism is proven, and the
safety properties hold under a real positive and real negative controls". That is real progress.

It does not change the verdict, because the shipped configuration still cannot detect a single
cheat client, and no behaviour-based detection exists. The plugin is a well-tested, fail-closed
**mod identity diagnostic**. Shipping it as an anti-cheat would advertise a capability the shipped
catalog does not have.

`docs/testing/P37-TERRAIN-MASK.md`:

```md
# P37 TerrainMask verification record

**Status: PARTIAL — entity concealment/restoration and required live visual acceptance are incomplete.**

## Implementation audit

TerrainMask uses the existing PacketEvents 2.14.0 bridge. It registers one outgoing listener after PacketEvents initialization and does not add another packet library or initializer. The listener uses the recipient UUID and immutable per-connection view snapshot; it does not read Bukkit world/player state on the packet callback.

For configured viewers, outgoing chunk data is decoded as a PacketEvents `Column`, snapshotted per recipient, copied and rewritten, then published through that same send event's replacement wrapper and re-encode flag. Each recipient gets an independent render from the retained real snapshot. The block ID is resolved from the recipient's `ClientVersion` registry, with startup preflight against Paper 1.21.11 and an automated protocol mapping test. AIR, cave-air, and void-air IDs are resolved per protocol. Section palettes/counts and biome payloads are preserved; hidden block entities are filtered; heightmaps and light are sanitized. Missing/invalid sections, heightmaps, mappings, cache capacity, or sensitive packet rewrites fail closed and mark diagnostics ERROR rather than forwarding an unrewritten chunk.

Later single- and multi-block updates update the recipient's retained real snapshot; underground block changes are rewritten for masked recipients. Block-entity and light updates are recorded/updated for transition replay. The source world is never changed by the rewrite code.

## Packet coverage and limitations

| Path | Current behavior | Evidence level |
|---|---|---|
| Initial chunk sections and section boundaries | Recipient-specific copy; positions below cutoff become configured fake block; AIR variants included when `hide-air` is on | UNIT-TESTED |
| Protocol block-state IDs | Resolved using PacketEvents state mappings for recipient protocol; DEEPSLATE mapping equality tested for 1.21.11 | UNIT-TESTED; startup previously tested separately |
| Heightmaps and biome payload | Heightmaps clamped to the synthetic concealed surface; biome data copied through | UNIT-TESTED |
| Block entities and light | Hidden block entities removed/cancelled and retained for replay; concealed light masks/arrays sanitized | UNIT-TESTED |
| Later block updates | Single/multi packet handling updates cached real section and rewrites hidden positions | UNIT-TESTED at payload/rewrite level; live packets NOT TESTED |
| Block actions, break animation, effects, particles, positional sounds | Underground/overlapping effects cancelled only for the masked recipient | Code-audited; live packets NOT TESTED |
| Explosion | Modern center/strength packet conservatively cancelled if its estimated radius reaches the hidden range | UNIT-TESTED policy; live packet NOT TESTED |
| Sculk vibration | Cancelled for masked recipient because its destination/source codec is not transformed | Code-audited; live packet NOT TESTED |
| Entity-attached sounds | Cancelled for masked recipient because the packet has an entity ID but no position | Code-audited; live packet NOT TESTED |
| Entity spawn, metadata, equipment, pose, movement, teleport, removal and restoration | **Unsupported.** These packets are not tracked or concealed. A masked viewer may receive entity state; a reveal transition does not replay a complete authoritative entity state. | NOT TESTED / NOT IMPLEMENTED |

The entity limitation is architectural, not a missing assertion: cancelling spawn/follow-up packets would desynchronize the client, while restoration needs entity identity, latest metadata/equipment/pose/position, and correct ordering with destroy/spawn packets. Paper `hideEntity/showEntity` can hide a known target for one viewer, but this service has no bounded tracker for entities in the viewer's relevant regions and no Folia-safe discovery/ownership handoff for targets that cross regions. Implementing that safely requires a dedicated lifecycle component and real Paper/Folia transition tests; no Bukkit entity calls were added from packet threads. Diagnostics report DEGRADED when entity hiding is configured.

Other position-bearing protocols not explicitly handled (including entity spawn/follow-up packets and any future PacketEvents packet types) are not covered merely because the listener is registered. Freecam visual access is not proven by these packet-level tests.

## State, scheduling, and bounds

- Mask state is based on the server-side player feet Y: `Y > mask-when-player-above-y` masks; `Y <=` reveals.
- Player/world state is updated from join, movement, respawn, and world-change events. Refresh replay reads the current immutable view, not the state captured when queued.
- Refreshes are submitted on the player's entity scheduler in bounded per-tick batches; the queue limit must be at least the cache limit. Cache overflow suppresses an uncached chunk rather than evicting a loaded snapshot.
- Quit, world change, and shutdown clear connection snapshots/queues. Packet callbacks contain no Bukkit world/player access.
- Bedrock masking is opt-in. A known BEDROCK or UNKNOWN classification is exempt unless enabled.
- No per-entity polling task or global entity removal is used.

## Evidence boundary

Unit fixtures do not establish recipient isolation on real sockets, client rendering, or Freecam visibility. The earlier Paper startup smoke only established plugin initialization/preflight; it is not live visual proof. P37 is not complete until a current built JAR passes the two-viewer same-chunk test and threshold/update checks on real clients. Freecam must be reported separately; it is NOT TESTED unless a compatible Freecam client is visually exercised.

## Live campaign record (2026-10-12, isolated Paper 1.21.11 + PacketEvents 2.14.0 server)

Test world (built deterministically through the console, verified block-by-block): a 48x48
stone mass from y=-32 to y=-1 with a 3x3 checker of gold/emerald/diamond on the y=-1
surface, an 8x8x8 room carved at x=6..13/z=6..13/y=-8..-1 with amethyst walls, striped
gold/diamond/emerald/lapis floor, chest, 4 torches, armor stand "P37CAVE", a stone tower
with a y=5 platform for the above-ground viewer, and a 21x21 y=19 plateau used only for
one fresh-join scenario (removed afterwards). Two vanilla Fabric clients plus one Meteor
1.21.11 Freecam client, all in chunk (0,0), server-confirmed positions.

Two defects were found live and fixed, each with a regression test:

1. **Double-read of event wrappers.** Every handler called `read()` after event
   construction, but PacketEvents constructors already decode once; the second read
   over-ran the buffer and every chunk was suppressed (fail-closed, clients stuck on
   loading). Fix: use event-constructed wrappers directly. Regression:
   `TerrainMaskEventRoundTripTest` (true wire-bytes round trip through a synthetic
   send event, asserting single-construction decode plus that a second read fails).
2. **Teleports invisible to the mask.** `PlayerTeleportEvent` has its own handler
   list, so the `PlayerMoveEvent` handler never saw teleports and mask state went
   stale across them. Fix: explicit teleport funnel. Regression: teleport flip and
   same-level-teleport no-op tests.
3. **Join-event location predates spawn positioning.** A fresh join reported y=0.0
   while the player settled at y=6/y=20, leaving initial chunks unmasked with no
   later correction (teleports did not fire the move handler either). Fix: two
   bounded one-shot join resyncs (+2/+10 ticks, entity-thread hop, abort on
   connection mismatch) that re-read the settled position; any staleness
   self-heals through the normal transition path. Regression: pre-spawn join
   corrected on settle, stale resync abort after quit/reconnect.

Observed live (screenshots in the run evidence set, server log counters):

- Masked viewer (feet y=6..20): uniform deepslate below y=0, pit opening capped,
  no gold/emerald/diamond/amethyst/chest shapes; AIR hidden (solid cap).
- Revealed viewer (feet y<=5, same chunk): real distinctive blocks, open pit,
  chest, armor stand, torches; server block changes (redstone/gold/fill) and a
  real creative-mode mine-through appear for B while A stays deepslate; world
  blocks verified real by console queries.
- Transitions both directions via teleport, fall (per-tick trace across y=5),
  respawn (both directions), world change to/from nether (cache cleared, fresh
  sends, no stale refresh), reconnect (fresh masked sends), `vac reload`
  (terrain untouched, transitions still fire). Bounded refresh drains to zero,
  zero rewrite/refresh failures across all runs.
- Real Meteor Freecam: body fixed at y=6 (server-confirmed), camera driven below
  y=0 through the room volume sees only solid mass/deepslate, never room detail;
  cap looks solid from above; freecam off restores the normal masked view; chat,
  inventory, hotbar unaffected.
- Entity packets are NOT concealed (armor stand visible to B; would also be sent
  to A): entity concealment/restoration remain unimplemented, diagnostics stay
  DEGRADED when configured. This is the release blocker for the entity phases.

`docs/testing/P38-ENTITY-VISION.md`:

```md
# P38 Entity Concealment, Restoration & Zero-Leak Join

## Design record

### Zero-leak join (Phase 2)

The join event can report a provisional position (observed: y=0.0 for a spawn that
settles at y=6 or y=20) before spawn positioning completes. The first chunks could
therefore be delivered with an unmasked view and no later correction (a delayed resync
only repairs the view; it cannot undeliver bytes).

Fix: `TerrainMaskService.update` takes `positionTrusted`. Only the join path passes
untrusted; every other path (resync, move, teleport, respawn, world change) passes
trusted. An eligible viewer with an untrusted position starts masked (fail closed).
Exempt, bypassed, and unconfigured joins are unaffected. The existing join resyncs
release the provisional state once the settled position is known: an underground
joiner briefly sees fake terrain, then gets the real replay through the normal
transition path. No chunks are loaded to decide this; it is purely time/position based.

### Entity concealment (Phases 3-4)

Mechanism: Paper per-viewer `hideEntity`/`showEntity`, verified against the
1.21.11 implementation. Hiding removes the viewer from the server tracker (destroy is
sent) and records our plugin; the tracking tick consults that record on every
attempt, so concealment persists with zero further traffic. Showing removes our
record and re-runs the tracker's own pairing step, re-sending complete current
state — restoration without synthetic packets, duplicates impossible (`seenBy`
guard), stale state impossible (server truth). Both calls are idempotent; showing a
never-hidden entity and hiding an already-hidden entity touch nothing (no tracker
writes, no events fired).

Three cooperating paths (every entity-to-client packet flows from tracker
membership, so these cover delivery completely):

1. **Track gate** (`PlayerTrackEntityEvent`, cancellable, respected by the tracker):
   inside the pairing step before any spawn bytes exist. Covers spawns, chunk
   loads, logins, and range entries. Records concealment, then cancels.
2. **Motion evaluation** (living moves, vehicle moves, teleports): re-decides on
   Y-crossings of the concealment cutoff while already tracked.
3. **Transition sweeps** (mask flips, world arrivals): reconciles nearby
   below-cutoff entities one by one on their own schedulers with full
   revalidation inside each task (liveness, world, cutoff, mask, connection
   token). Bounded at 512 candidates per sweep with a truncation counter.

State: none per entity. Every deferred task revalidates; quit removes the
connection so pending tasks abort; removal makes tasks abort via `isValid`;
reconnect creates fresh player objects with clean visibility maps. Repeated
hide/show calls collapse through a `canSee` gate, so steady-state motion is
cheap and counters count actual flips.

Threading: all hide/show runs on the subject entity's owning scheduler (motion
and track events already run there). Tracker structures stay on owning threads;
viewer lookups are map reads. The CraftBukkit visibility map is unsynchronized,
so same-viewer concurrent updates from different entity threads can race a
single entry; the impact is bounded to one entity's visibility and self-heals
on the next entity event or viewer flip. Exact on Paper (single thread);
documented heuristic on Folia. No Bukkit entity/player access from packet
threads (packet layer only counts spawn positions, never mutates).

Deliberate non-goals: entities with `isVisibleByDefault() == false` (managed by
other plugins) are left alone; shutdown does a best-effort unhide sweep so a
same-process re-enable starts clean (any residue clears on reconnect); a
same-process runtime plugin reload with connected players is not tested.

### Side-channel review (Phase 6)

Cutoffs: blocks below `hide-below-y` (0), viewers masked above
`mask-when-player-above-y` (5). Ratings are for a masked viewer.

| Path | Rating | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Initial chunk sections | PROTECTED | Per-recipient rewrite incl. AIR when configured; fail-closed |
| Heightmaps | PROTECTED | Clamped to synthetic surface |
| Single/multi block updates | PROTECTED | Snapshot updated + rewritten for masked |
| Block-entity data | PROTECTED | Hidden ones cancelled for masked, retained for replay |
| Light updates | PROTECTED | Sanitized below cutoff for masked |
| Entity spawn/destroy | PROTECTED | Track gate cancels spawn to masked; destroy only sent to trackers |
| Entity movement/teleport | PROTECTED | Motion path re-decides on cutoff crossing; tracked deltas only reach trackers |
| Entity metadata/equipment | PROTECTED | Tracker-membership only; restoration re-sends current state |
| Mounts/attachments | PARTIALLY PROTECTED | Vehicle hidden as a unit; passenger rendering follows the vehicle packet the client holds |
| Entity effects/attributes | PROTECTED | Same tracker-membership delivery |
| Entity-associated sounds | PROTECTED | Blanket-suppressed for masked viewers (over-suppression, no leak possible) |
| Positional sounds/particles | PROTECTED | Suppressed below cutoff for masked |
| Explosions/block-break effects | PROTECTED | Conservative radius cancel / position cancel for masked |
| Sculk vibration | PROTECTED | Cancelled for masked (codec not transformed) |
| Player tab list | PARTIALLY PROTECTED | Hidden underground players also drop from the masked viewer's tab list (inherent to hideEntity; consistent confidentiality) |
| Non-living gradual motion | PARTIALLY PROTECTED | No Bukkit motion event exists; covered on next tracked event, sweep, or flip; masked-above sweep heals stale hides |
| Third-party runtime reload | NOT APPLICABLE | Paper 1.21.11 `/reload` does not touch plugins; same-process reloaders untested |

### Evidence boundary

Unit tests prove dispatch decisions, bounds, cleanup, and codec behavior. Only the
live two-client + Freecam runs prove recipient isolation and restoration on real
sockets. Folia is unit-tested for scheduler ownership only, never live.

```

# Probe Validation Matrix

Every one of the 42 catalogued probes, generated from `client-detection.yml` and cross-checked
against the coverage matrix by `ClientCoverageMatrixTest`, `InventoryGuardTest`,
`ProbeValidityMatrixTest` and `ShippedConfigurationTest`.

Status labels: `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED_NOT_AVAILABLE`, `NOT_APPLICABLE`, `NOT_TESTED`.

**The UNIT / INTEGRATION / LIVE columns are deliberately separate.** A `PASS` in the UNIT column
means the evaluator classified a *simulated* response correctly. It is **not** evidence that a real
client produces that response. Only the LIVE column records a real client session, and only one
probe has one.

> **UPDATED BY PHASE II (2026-10-09).** Three material changes:
>
> 1. The **interactive transport is confirmed working** against a real client (~95 ms response,
>    `outcome=RESPONSE`, full 24-probe batch with `noResponse=0`). Phase I marked it
>    `BLOCKED_NOT_AVAILABLE` from a measurement error.
> 2. **`xaeros-minimap` and `xaeros-worldmap` are now `LIVE_VERIFIED`.** A real client returned
>    exactly `"Minimap"` and `"Open World Map"`; both reported `status=DETECTED evidence=STRONG`
>    and corroborated into a single BLOCKED verdict. LIVE column changes FAIL/BLOCKED → PASS.
> 3. **`meteor-client` changes from `FAIL` to `BLOCKED_NOT_AVAILABLE`.** The mechanism works and
>    Meteor returned `"Open GUI"`, but the probe deliberately declares no expected response, so
>    the shipped catalog has no route. That is a safety decision, not a broken detector.
>
> Full evidence in [`DETECTION-AND-ENFORCEMENT.md`](DETECTION-AND-ENFORCEMENT.md).

## How each column was produced

- **UNIT** — `ProbeCatalogExecutionTest` (380 parameterised cases, one per probe per scenario) runs
  every probe through the same `CheckHacksResponseEvaluator` production code uses. JUnit fails if the
  parameterised factory and the catalog disagree, so a new probe is covered automatically.
- **INTEGRATION** — the passive transport and scan lifecycle are covered by
  `P33PassiveDetectionTest`, `P34JoinPassiveLifecycleTest`, `PaperSignProbeTransportTest`,
  `ThreePlayerIsolationTest` and `ClientResponseSimulationTest`. These use fake players and a
  disposable transport; they are not real clients.
- **LIVE** — a real Fabric 1.21.11 client on a real Paper 1.21.11 server. See
  [`REAL-CLIENT-RESULTS.md`](REAL-CLIENT-RESULTS.md).

## Scenario coverage applied to every probe

Applicable scenarios from the campaign, mapped onto the per-probe suite:

| # | Scenario | Applied as | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1, 2 | Intended signal present / absent | sentinel response always CLEAN and non-authoritative | PASS (all 42) |
| 3 | Client does not support the check | empty and blank responses never DETECTED | PASS (all 42) |
| 4 | Player disconnects during the check | `DISCONNECTED` and `ERROR` map to `ERROR`, never DETECTED | PASS (all 42) |
| 5 | Response never arrives | `TIMEOUT` → `TIMEOUT` + `NO_EVIDENCE` basis | PASS (all 42) |
| 6 | Response arrives after timeout | covered by the timeout-streak tests in the transport suite | PASS |
| 7 | Duplicate / malformed / unexpected response | 7 hostile inputs per probe: empty, `;;;`, script tag, 4 KiB string, NUL-padded key, upper-cased key, truncated key — none may be promoted | PASS (all 42) |
| 8 | Reconnect with earlier state present | connection-identity comparison in `ClientSignalCollector`; live-verified for the passive probe | PASS |
| 9 | Repeated requests and cancellation races | transport callback de-duplication and the fixed queue-drain harness | PASS |
| 10 | Concurrent players, same probe | `ThreePlayerIsolationTest`; **live-verified** with two simultaneous clients | PASS |
| 11 | Reload / shutdown with work pending | reload preserves passive state and retired floor; live `vac reload` observed | PASS |
| 12 | Unknown / unclassified evidence | `ProbeCorroboration.basisOf` returns `UNCLASSIFIED` and is never authoritative | PASS |
| 13 | Multiple conflicting evidence sources | conflicting DETECTED blocks are removed from `promoted` | PASS |
| 14 | Legitimate mod must not be classified as a cheat | category gate; **live-verified** for Jade, Xaero pair, AppleSkin | PASS |
| 15 | Disabled probes and non-automatic probes | `disabledProbesAreNeverEligible`, `onlyPassiveProbeIsAutomaticEligibleByDefault` | PASS (all 42) |
