`src/main/java/site/vackstudio/vanticheat/lunar/LunarPolicyConfig.java`:

```java
package site.vackstudio.vanticheat.lunar;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.logging.Level;
import java.util.logging.Logger;

/**
 * Server policy for Lunar Client Apollo integration.
 *
 * <p>Lunar Client itself is always allowed. Only the Lunar Minimap can be
 * disabled via Apollo, and only for players Apollo recognizes. This config
 * never produces kicks or cheat classifications.
 */
public record LunarPolicyConfig(boolean enabled, boolean minimapEnabled) {
    public static LunarPolicyConfig defaults() {
        return new LunarPolicyConfig(true, true);
    }

    public static LunarPolicyConfig disabled() {
        return new LunarPolicyConfig(false, false);
    }

    public static LunarPolicyConfig load(Path dataDirectory, Logger logger) {
        if (dataDirectory == null) return disabled();
        Path file = dataDirectory.resolve("config.yml");
        if (!Files.isRegularFile(file)) return defaults();
        try {
            return parse(Files.readString(file));
        } catch (IOException | RuntimeException exception) {
            logger.log(Level.WARNING,
                    "Unable to load lunar policy from config.yml; lunar integration disabled", exception);
            return disabled();
        }
    }

    static LunarPolicyConfig parse(String content) {
        boolean enabled = true;
        boolean minimapEnabled = true;
        boolean inLunar = false;
        boolean inMinimap = false;
        for (String rawLine : content.split("\\R")) {
            String line = rawLine.stripTrailing();
            if (line.isBlank() || line.stripLeading().startsWith("#")) continue;
            int indent = line.length() - line.stripLeading().length();
            String trimmed = line.trim();
            if (indent == 0) {
                inLunar = trimmed.equals("lunar:");
                inMinimap = false;
                continue;
            }
            if (!inLunar) continue;
            if (indent == 2) {
                if (trimmed.equals("minimap:")) {
                    inMinimap = true;
                    continue;
                }
                inMinimap = false;
                String[] pair = pair(trimmed, "lunar");
                if (pair[0].equals("enabled")) enabled = bool(pair[1], "lunar.enabled");
                continue;
            }
            if (indent >= 4 && inMinimap) {
                String[] pair = pair(trimmed, "lunar.minimap");
                switch (pair[0]) {
                    case "enabled" -> minimapEnabled = bool(pair[1], "lunar.minimap.enabled");
                    case "action" -> {
                        if (!pair[1].equalsIgnoreCase("DISABLE")) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                                    "Unsupported value at lunar.minimap.action: '" + pair[1]
                                            + "'; only DISABLE is supported");
                        }
                    }
                    default -> { }
                }
            }
        }
        return new LunarPolicyConfig(enabled, minimapEnabled);
    }

    private static String[] pair(String value, String path) {
        String[] pair = value.split(":", 2);
        if (pair.length != 2) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid config entry at " + path);
        return new String[]{pair[0].trim(), unquote(pair[1].trim())};
    }

    private static boolean bool(String value, String path) {
        if (value.equalsIgnoreCase("true")) return true;
        if (value.equalsIgnoreCase("false")) return false;
        throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                "Expected boolean at " + path + " but was '" + value + "'");
    }

    private static String unquote(String value) {
        if (value.length() >= 2 && ((value.startsWith("\"") && value.endsWith("\""))
                || (value.startsWith("'") && value.endsWith("'")))) {
            return value.substring(1, value.length() - 1);
        }
        return value;
    }
}

```

`src/main/java/site/vackstudio/vanticheat/modlist/ForgeModListParser.java`:

```java
package site.vackstudio.vanticheat.modlist;

import java.io.ByteArrayInputStream;
import java.io.DataInputStream;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;

/**
 * Parses the Forge FML handshake mod list, which is the only mod list a Minecraft client sends
 * to a game server.
 *
 * <p><b>Wire format</b>, from the FML handshake specification and Velocity's own parser:
 *
 * <pre>
 *   byte    discriminator  must equal {@link #MOD_LIST_DISCRIMINATOR} (2)
 *   varint  mod count
 *   repeat mod count times:
 *     string mod id      (varint length, UTF-8 bytes)
 *     string mod version (varint length, UTF-8 bytes)
 * </pre>
 *
 * <p><b>Fabric clients never reach this class.</b> Fabric Loader transmits no mod list to a game
 * server, so a Fabric client produces no parseable payload here and no result. That is a protocol
 * fact, not a failure: nothing in this class can be made to cover Fabric.
 *
 * <p><b>Every method is total over hostile input.</b> The payload arrives from an unconnected,
 * unauthenticated client, so it is attacker-controlled by definition. A client controls the varint
 * count and the declared string lengths, and both are bounded here before anything proportional to
 * them is allocated. A count of 2,000,000,000 or a string claiming 2 GB must not become an
 * allocation attempt; it must become a refusal.
 *
 * <p>This class is pure: no Bukkit, no PacketEvents, no network, no clock. That keeps the parsing
 * logic testable against hand-built byte arrays, which is the only honest way to test a wire
 * format.
 */
public final class ForgeModListParser {
    /**
     * The FML|HS discriminator that marks a client-to-server mod list (legacy, 1.8-1.12).
     *
     * <p>This is a raw <b>byte</b>, and it is not the same value type as the modern discriminator.
     */
    public static final int LEGACY_MOD_LIST_DISCRIMINATOR = 2;

    /**
     * The {@code fml:handshake} message index for a client mod list (modern, 1.13+).
     *
     * <p>Modern Forge runs the handshake over a SimpleChannel, which prefixes every message with a
     * <b>varint</b> index. Reading it as a byte would misparse it.
     */
    public static final int MODERN_MOD_LIST_INDEX = 2;

    /**
     * Upper bound on the declared mod count, matching Velocity's own cap.
     *
     * <p>The count is a varint the client chose. Without a cap, a hostile client declares
     * {@code Integer.MAX_VALUE} mods and the parser attempts to allocate for each one before the
     * payload even runs out of bytes.
     */
    public static final int MAX_MOD_COUNT = 1024;

    /** Upper bound on any single mod id or version string, in bytes. */
    public static final int MAX_STRING_BYTES = 256;

    /**
     * Upper bound on the whole payload, in bytes.
     *
     * <p>A legitimate mod list is a few kilobytes. Anything past this is not a mod list, and
     * refusing it costs nothing because a refusal is never a detection.
     */
    public static final int MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 64 * 1024;

    /** Legacy Forge handshake channel. */
    public static final String LEGACY_CHANNEL = "FML|HS";

    /** Modern Forge handshake channel. */
    public static final String MODERN_CHANNEL = "fml:handshake";

    private ForgeModListParser() {
    }

    /** Both handshake channels a Forge client may use. */
    public static Set<String> handshakeChannels() {
        return Set.of(LEGACY_CHANNEL, MODERN_CHANNEL);
    }

    /** True when the channel is one a Forge client uses for the handshake. */
    public static boolean isHandshakeChannel(String channel) {
        return LEGACY_CHANNEL.equals(channel) || MODERN_CHANNEL.equals(channel);
    }

    /**
     * Which wire format a channel carries.
     *
     * <p>This distinction is not cosmetic. The two formats share a discriminator value of 2 and
     * nothing else:
     *
     * <pre>
     *   legacy FML|HS   byte(2)          varint count   { string id, string version } * count
     *   modern handshake varint(2)       varint count   string id * count,
     *                                                   varint channelCount { string, string } *,
     *                                                   varint registryCount string *
     * </pre>
     *
     * <p>Parsing a modern payload with the legacy layout pairs each id with the <i>next id</i> and
     * treats it as a version, then runs off the end of the list into the channel map. That yields
     * plausible-looking garbage rather than an error, which is the worst possible failure mode for
     * an enforcement decision: it could match a denied id that was never installed.
     *
     * <p>So the channel selects the layout. There is no auto-detection, because auto-detection
     * would have to guess between two formats that both begin with the same number.
     */
    public enum WireFormat {
        /** {@code FML|HS}: byte discriminator, id + version pairs. */
        LEGACY,
        /** {@code fml:handshake}: varint index, ids only, then channels and registries. */
        MODERN
    }

    /**
     * Resolves the wire format for a channel.
     *
     * @return null when the channel is not a Forge handshake channel, so an unrelated channel is
     *         ignored rather than guessed at.
     */
    public static WireFormat formatFor(String channel) {
        if (LEGACY_CHANNEL.equals(channel)) return WireFormat.LEGACY;
        if (MODERN_CHANNEL.equals(channel)) return WireFormat.MODERN;
        return null;
    }

    /** What a parse attempt produced. Never a detection on its own. */
    public sealed interface Result {
        /**
         * The payload was a client mod list, and these mods were declared.
         *
         * <p>Iteration order is the order the client declared, because {@code Map.copyOf} does not
         * preserve it and mod lists are logged and rendered in that order.
         *
         * <p>For the modern format the version component is absent, because that wire format does
         * not carry one. Every value is then the empty string rather than a guess, so no downstream
         * consumer can present a fabricated version to an operator.
         */
        record Parsed(java.util.Map<String, String> mods, WireFormat format) implements Result { }

        /**
         * The payload was well-formed but not a mod list.
         *
         * <p>Almost every Forge handshake packet is this. This is the normal case, not a problem.
         */
        record NotAModList(int discriminator) implements Result { }

        /**
         * The payload was malformed or exceeded a bound, and was refused.
         *
         * <p>Never actionable. A client can send garbage here, so a refusal is a statement about
         * the bytes, never about the player's software.
         */
        record Refused(String reason) implements Result { }
    }

    /**
     * Parses one handshake payload, using the wire format implied by its channel.
     *
     * <p>Total: never throws, never allocates proportionally to an untrusted declared length.
     */
    public static Result parse(String channel, byte[] payload) {
        WireFormat format = formatFor(channel);
        if (format == null) {
            return new Result.Refused("not a forge handshake channel");
        }
        if (payload == null || payload.length == 0) {
            return new Result.Refused("empty payload");
        }
        if (payload.length > MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES) {
            return new Result.Refused("payload " + payload.length + " exceeds "
                    + MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES + " bytes");
        }
        try (DataInputStream in = new DataInputStream(new ByteArrayInputStream(payload))) {
            return format == WireFormat.LEGACY ? parseLegacy(in) : parseModern(in);
        } catch (IOException | RuntimeException malformed) {
            return new Result.Refused(malformed.getClass().getSimpleName());
        }
    }

    /**
     * Legacy {@code FML|HS}: byte discriminator, then id/version pairs.
     *
     * <p>Used by Minecraft 1.8 through 1.12. A 1.21.11 server cannot be reached by such a client,
     * so this path exists for protocol completeness and for tests, not for the shipped game version.
     */
    private static Result parseLegacy(DataInputStream in) throws IOException {
        int discriminator = in.readUnsignedByte();
        if (discriminator != LEGACY_MOD_LIST_DISCRIMINATOR) {
            return new Result.NotAModList(discriminator);
        }
        int count = readVarInt(in);
        String tooLarge = rejectCount(count);
        if (tooLarge != null) return new Result.Refused(tooLarge);

        Map<String, String> mods = new LinkedHashMap<>(Math.min(count, 64));
        for (int index = 0; index < count; index++) {
            String id = readBoundedString(in);
            if (id == null) return new Result.Refused("mod id unreadable at index " + index);
            String version = readBoundedString(in);
            if (version == null) {
                return new Result.Refused("mod version unreadable at index " + index);
            }
            mods.put(id, version);
        }
        return new Result.Parsed(java.util.Collections.unmodifiableMap(mods), WireFormat.LEGACY);
    }

    /**
     * Modern {@code fml:handshake}: varint message index, then ids only, then the channel map and
     * registry list.
     *
     * <p>This is the format a Minecraft 1.21.11 Forge client actually sends, so it is the path that
     * matters in production.
     *
     * <p>The trailing channel map and registry list are read and discarded. They are not mod ids,
     * they cannot match the denylist, and retaining them would store channel metadata the plugin
     * has no use for. They are still bounded: a hostile client can declare a huge channel count, so
     * it is capped and validated exactly like the mod count.
     */
    private static Result parseModern(DataInputStream in) throws IOException {
        int index = readVarInt(in);
        if (index < 0) {
            return new Result.Refused("varint message index malformed");
        }
        if (index != MODERN_MOD_LIST_INDEX) {
            return new Result.NotAModList(index);
        }
        int count = readVarInt(in);
        String tooLarge = rejectCount(count);
        if (tooLarge != null) return new Result.Refused(tooLarge);

        Map<String, String> mods = new LinkedHashMap<>(Math.min(count, 64));
        for (int entry = 0; entry < count; entry++) {
            String id = readBoundedString(in);
            if (id == null) return new Result.Refused("mod id unreadable at index " + entry);
            // The modern format carries no version. Empty, never fabricated.
            mods.put(id, "");
        }
        if (!consumeModernTail(in)) {
            return new Result.Refused("modern channel/registry section malformed");
        }
        return new Result.Parsed(java.util.Collections.unmodifiableMap(mods), WireFormat.MODERN);
    }

    /**
     * Reads and discards the channel map and registry list that follow the modern mod list.
     *
     * <p>Validated and bounded rather than ignored blindly: the counts are client-chosen, so an
     * unchecked skip loop could spin on a huge declared count.
     *
     * @return false when the section is malformed or exceeds a bound
     */
    private static boolean consumeModernTail(DataInputStream in) throws IOException {
        int channelCount = readVarInt(in);
        if (channelCount < 0) return false;
        if (channelCount > MAX_MOD_COUNT) return false;
        for (int index = 0; index < channelCount; index++) {
            if (readBoundedString(in) == null) return false;  // channel name
            if (readBoundedString(in) == null) return false;  // channel marker
        }
        int registryCount = readVarInt(in);
        if (registryCount < 0) return false;
        if (registryCount > MAX_MOD_COUNT) return false;
        for (int index = 0; index < registryCount; index++) {
            if (readBoundedString(in) == null) return false;  // registry identifier
        }
        return true;
    }

    /** Shared count validation, so both formats refuse identically. */
    private static String rejectCount(int count) {
        if (count < 0) return "varint count malformed";
        if (count > MAX_MOD_COUNT) {
            // Refuse before allocating anything sized by the count.
            return "declared mod count " + count + " exceeds " + MAX_MOD_COUNT;
        }
        return null;
    }

    /**
     * Reads a length-prefixed string, refusing any declared length beyond {@link #MAX_STRING_BYTES}.
     *
     * <p>Returns null on any failure so the caller refuses the whole payload. Returning an empty
     * string instead would let a truncated payload masquerade as a mod named "".
     */
    private static String readBoundedString(DataInputStream in) throws IOException {
        int length = readVarInt(in);
        if (length < 0 || length > MAX_STRING_BYTES) {
            throw new IOException("string length " + length + " out of bounds");
        }
        if (length == 0) {
            return "";
        }
        byte[] bytes = new byte[length];
        in.readFully(bytes);
        // Decoding is bounded by MAX_STRING_BYTES, so this cannot allocate proportionally to a
        // hostile claim. Malformed UTF-8 raises, which the caller turns into a refusal.
        return new String(bytes, java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    }

    private static int readVarInt(DataInputStream in) throws IOException {
        int value = 0;
        int shift = 0;
        for (int read = 0; read < 5; read++) {
            int b = in.read();
            if (b < 0) {
                return -1;
            }
            value |= (b & 0x7F) << shift;
            if ((b & 0x80) == 0) {
                return value;
            }
            shift += 7;
        }
        return -1;
    }

    /**
     * Builds a legacy {@code FML|HS} mod-list payload.
     *
     * <p><b>Synthetic.</b> Hand-built from the documented wire format to exercise the parser; it is
     * not captured client traffic and must not be presented as such.
     */
    public static byte[] encodeLegacyForTest(List<String[]> mods) {
        java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream out = new java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream();
        out.write(LEGACY_MOD_LIST_DISCRIMINATOR);
        writeVarInt(out, mods.size());
        for (String[] mod : mods) {
            writeString(out, mod[0]);
            writeString(out, mod[1]);
        }
        return out.toByteArray();
    }

    /**
     * Builds a modern {@code fml:handshake} mod-list-reply payload.
     *
     * <p><b>Synthetic.</b> Modelled on {@code HandshakeMessages.C2SModListReply}: varint index, ids
     * only, then an empty channel map and registry list. It exists to prove the modern layout is
     * read with the modern layout, which is the defect this replaced.
     */
    public static byte[] encodeModernForTest(List<String> modIds) {
        java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream out = new java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream();
        writeVarInt(out, MODERN_MOD_LIST_INDEX);
        writeVarInt(out, modIds.size());
        for (String id : modIds) {
            writeString(out, id);
        }
        writeVarInt(out, 0); // channel count
        writeVarInt(out, 0); // registry count
        return out.toByteArray();
    }

    private static void writeVarInt(java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream out, int value) {
        while (true) {
            if ((value & ~0x7F) == 0) {
                out.write(value);
                return;
            }
            out.write((value & 0x7F) | 0x80);
            value >>>= 7;
        }
    }

    private static void writeString(java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream out, String text) {
        byte[] bytes = text.getBytes(java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        writeVarInt(out, bytes.length);
        out.writeBytes(bytes);
    }

    /** Convenience: the declared mod ids of a parsed payload, empty for anything else. */
    public static List<String> idsOf(Result result) {
        if (result instanceof Result.Parsed parsed) {
            return new ArrayList<>(parsed.mods().keySet());
        }
        return List.of();
    }
}
```

`src/main/java/site/vackstudio/vanticheat/modlist/ModListConnectionRegistry.java`:

```java
package site.vackstudio.vanticheat.modlist;

import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.UUID;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong;

/**
 * Connection-scoped state for Forge mod-list observation.
 *
 * <p><b>Why not keyed by UUID alone.</b> A UUID survives a reconnect. If state were keyed by UUID
 * with no connection identity, a second connection could inherit the first connection's parsed mod
 * list and be denied for a mod it never installed. That is a false positive produced entirely by
 * lifecycle bookkeeping, and it is the specific failure this class exists to prevent.
 *
 * <p>Every entry is therefore created with a fresh <b>connection token</b>. A decision is only ever
 * read for the token that produced it, and {@link #forget} removes the entry outright. A caller
 * holding a stale token gets {@code null}, never a previous connection's result.
 *
 * <p><b>Bounded.</b> The map is capped. A leak of unbounded per-connection entries would be a
 * memory exhaustion vector on a server that churns connections, so eviction is explicit and oldest-
 * first rather than left to the garbage collector.
 *
 * <p><b>Locking.</b> Packet callbacks arrive on Netty event-loop threads, potentially many
 * concurrently and not necessarily the same one, while disconnect cleanup can arrive on a Bukkit
 * thread. All state transitions are serialised on the instance monitor. No method blocks on I/O, so
 * the critical sections are a handful of map operations.
 */
public final class ModListConnectionRegistry {

    /** Maximum live tracked connections. Beyond this, the oldest entry is evicted. */
    public static final int MAX_TRACKED = 2048;

    /** One connection's observation state. */
    public static final class Entry {
        private final UUID playerId;
        private final long token;
        private final long startedAtMillis;
        private volatile ModListEnforcement.Observation observation;
        private volatile ModListEnforcement.Decision decision;
        private volatile boolean released;

        private Entry(UUID playerId, long token, long startedAtMillis) {
            this.playerId = playerId;
            this.token = token;
            this.startedAtMillis = startedAtMillis;
        }

        /** Identity of the connection that produced this entry. */
        public long token() {
            return token;
        }

        public UUID playerId() {
            return playerId;
        }

        public long startedAtMillis() {
            return startedAtMillis;
        }

        public ModListEnforcement.Observation observation() {
            return observation;
        }

        public ModListEnforcement.Decision decision() {
            return decision;
        }

        /** True once this connection's state has been released. */
        public boolean released() {
            return released;
        }
    }

    private final Map<UUID, Entry> live = new LinkedHashMap<>(64, 0.75f, false);
    private final AtomicLong tokens = new AtomicLong();
    private final LongSupplierHolder clock;

    /** Indirection so tests can drive time deterministically. */
    public interface LongSupplierHolder {
        long millis();
    }

    public ModListConnectionRegistry() {
        this(System::currentTimeMillis);
    }

    public ModListConnectionRegistry(java.util.function.LongSupplier clock) {
        this.clock = clock::getAsLong;
    }

    /**
     * Begins tracking a connection, replacing any previous entry for the same UUID.
     *
     * <p>A reconnect therefore starts from a clean state, which is what makes a stale decision
     * impossible rather than merely unlikely.
     */
    public synchronized Entry begin(UUID playerId) {
        if (playerId == null) {
            return null;
        }
        Entry entry = new Entry(playerId, tokens.incrementAndGet(), clock.millis());
        live.put(playerId, entry);
        evictIfNeeded();
        return entry;
    }

    /** The current entry for a UUID, or null when none is tracked. */
    public synchronized Entry current(UUID playerId) {
        return playerId == null ? null : live.get(playerId);
    }

    /** The entry only when it is the caller's own connection, so a stale token resolves to null. */
    public synchronized Entry current(UUID playerId, long token) {
        Entry entry = current(playerId);
        return entry != null && entry.token() == token ? entry : null;
    }

    /**
     * Records an observation for a connection.
     *
     * <p>Idempotent by token: a repeated handshake message cannot overwrite the first complete
     * observation, so a duplicate packet cannot change or re-trigger a decision.
     *
     * @return true when the observation was accepted, false when it was stale or already complete
     */
    public synchronized boolean observe(UUID playerId, long token,
                                        ModListEnforcement.Observation observation) {
        Entry entry = current(playerId, token);
        if (entry == null || entry.released) return false;
        ModListEnforcement.Observation existing = entry.observation;
        // First COMPLETE observation wins. A later duplicate is ignored rather than re-applied.
        if (existing != null && existing.status() == ModListEnforcement.ObservationStatus.COMPLETE) {
            return false;
        }
        entry.observation = observation;
        return true;
    }

    /** Records the decision for a connection. Idempotent: the first decision is terminal. */
    public synchronized boolean decide(UUID playerId, long token,
                                       ModListEnforcement.Decision decision) {
        Entry entry = current(playerId, token);
        if (entry == null || entry.released) return false;
        if (entry.decision != null) {
            // A second decision for the same connection would be a duplicate denial path.
            return false;
        }
        entry.decision = decision;
        return true;
    }

    /**
     * Releases connection state exactly once.
     *
     * <p>Safe to call from disconnect, denial, timeout, failure, and shutdown; a repeated call is
     * a no-op rather than an error, so cleanup paths can overlap without double-freeing.
     *
     * @return true when this call released the entry
     */
    public synchronized boolean forget(UUID playerId) {
        if (playerId == null) return false;
        Entry removed = live.remove(playerId);
        if (removed == null) return false;
        removed.released = true;
        return true;
    }

    /** Releases a specific connection only when the token still matches. */
    public synchronized boolean forget(UUID playerId, long token) {
        Entry entry = current(playerId, token);
        if (entry == null || entry.token() != token) return false;
        return forget(playerId);
    }

    /** Releases everything. Used on plugin disable and shutdown. */
    public synchronized int clear() {
        int count = live.size();
        for (Entry entry : live.values()) {
            entry.released = true;
        }
        live.clear();
        return count;
    }

    public synchronized int tracked() {
        return live.size();
    }

    /** Bounded-state guarantee: the registry never exceeds {@link #MAX_TRACKED}. */
    private void evictIfNeeded() {
        while (live.size() > MAX_TRACKED) {
            var iterator = live.entrySet().iterator();
            if (!iterator.hasNext()) return;
            Entry oldest = iterator.next().getValue();
            iterator.remove();
            oldest.released = true;
        }
    }
}
```

`src/main/java/site/vackstudio/vanticheat/modlist/ModListDenylist.java`:

```java
package site.vackstudio.vanticheat.modlist;

import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.LinkedHashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;

/**
 * Exact mod-id denylist for client mod lists.
 *
 * <p><b>Matching is exact, by deliberate design.</b> A mod is blocked only when its declared id
 * equals a configured id, byte for byte after lowercasing. No substring, prefix, suffix, or
 * "looks similar" matching is performed anywhere in this class, and none may be added: a substring
 * rule would let an unrelated mod whose name merely contains a blocked name be punished, and that
 * is the exact false-positive class this plugin exists to avoid. A player running a mod called
 * {@code notmeteor-client} is not running Meteor.
 *
 * <p><b>Ids are the only evidence.</b> A declared mod id is a fact the client asserted about its
 * own installation. It is not a heuristic, not a score, and not a guess. That is what makes an
 * exact match safe to act on where a translation-key match is not.
 *
 * <p><b>This class blocks nothing by itself.</b> It answers a question - "did this declared list
 * contain a configured id?" - and the caller decides what an answer means. Keeping the question
 * separate from the consequence is what lets the decision be tested, logged, and reviewed.
 */
public final class ModListDenylist {
    private final Set<String> blocked;
    private final Map<String, String> reason;

    private ModListDenylist(Set<String> blocked, Map<String, String> reason) {
        this.blocked = Set.copyOf(blocked);
        this.reason = Map.copyOf(reason);
    }

    public static ModListDenylist empty() {
        return new ModListDenylist(Set.of(), Map.of());
    }

    /**
     * Builds a denylist from configured ids.
     *
     * <p>Ids are normalised by trimming and lowercasing, because Forge ids are case-insensitive in
     * practice and a case difference must not become an escape. Blank entries are dropped, and a
     * malformed id is dropped with the rest rather than rejecting the whole configuration: one bad
     * line must not silently disable blocking for every other entry.
     */
    public static ModListDenylist of(Map<String, String> configured) {
        Set<String> ids = new LinkedHashSet<>();
        Map<String, String> reasons = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        if (configured != null) {
            configured.forEach((rawId, rawReason) -> {
                if (rawId == null) return;
                String id = normalize(rawId);
                if (id.isEmpty() || !isPlausibleId(id)) return;
                ids.add(id);
                reasons.put(id, rawReason == null ? "" : rawReason.trim());
            });
        }
        return new ModListDenylist(ids, reasons);
    }

    /** Builds a denylist from a bare id list, with no per-entry reason. */
    public static ModListDenylist ofIds(List<String> ids) {
        Map<String, String> map = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        if (ids != null) {
            for (String id : ids) {
                if (id != null) map.put(id, "");
            }
        }
        return of(map);
    }

    /**
     * A mod id is {@code [a-z0-9_.-]}.
     *
     * <p>This is the Fabric and Forge id grammar. Rejecting anything else stops a configured
     * glob-like entry such as {@code meteor*} from being stored and then matching by accident
     * later; such an entry could never match a real id anyway.
     */
    private static boolean isPlausibleId(String id) {
        return isCanonicalId(id);
    }

    public static String normalize(String raw) {
        return raw == null ? "" : raw.trim().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
    }

    /**
     * True when the value is a canonical Forge/Fabric mod id.
     *
     * <p>Public so the configuration validator and the matcher enforce the same grammar. Sharing one
     * definition is what stops a rule from being accepted by the loader and rejected at match time,
     * or worse, accepted by both.
     */
    public static boolean isCanonicalId(String id) {
        if (id == null || id.isEmpty()) return false;
        for (int index = 0; index < id.length(); index++) {
            char c = id.charAt(index);
            boolean allowed = (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9')
                    || c == '_' || c == '-' || c == '.';
            if (!allowed) return false;
        }
        return true;
    }

    /** What a denylist check found. */
    public record Match(String modId, String version, String reason) {
        /** Single-line rendering for logs and status output. Never contains raw client input. */
        @Override
        public String toString() {
            String suffix = reason == null || reason.isBlank() ? "" : " (" + reason + ")";
            return modId + suffix;
        }
    }

    /** Every blocked id present in the declared list, in declaration order. */
    public java.util.List<Match> findMatches(Map<String, String> declaredMods) {
        if (declaredMods == null || declaredMods.isEmpty() || blocked.isEmpty()) {
            return List.of();
        }
        java.util.List<Match> matches = new java.util.ArrayList<>();
        for (Map.Entry<String, String> entry : declaredMods.entrySet()) {
            String id = normalize(entry.getKey());
            if (!id.isEmpty() && blocked.contains(id)) {
                matches.add(new Match(id, entry.getValue(), reason.get(id)));
            }
        }
        return List.copyOf(matches);
    }

    public boolean isBlocked(String modId) {
        String id = normalize(modId);
        return !id.isEmpty() && blocked.contains(id);
    }

    public boolean blocksAny(Map<String, String> declaredMods) {
        return !findMatches(declaredMods).isEmpty();
    }

    public Set<String> blockedIds() {
        return blocked;
    }

    public int size() {
        return blocked.size();
    }
}
```

`src/main/java/site/vackstudio/vanticheat/modlist/ModListDenylistConfig.java`:

```java
package site.vackstudio.vanticheat.modlist;

import org.bukkit.configuration.ConfigurationSection;
import org.bukkit.configuration.file.YamlConfiguration;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.logging.Logger;

/**
 * Loads {@code modlist-denylist.yml}.
 *
 * <p><b>Shipped empty and enabled-but-inert.</b> The default configuration denies nobody: the
 * denylist contains no ids, and an operator adds them deliberately after verifying each id against
 * a real client. A feature that denies nobody out of the box cannot kick a legitimate player by
 * mistake.
 *
 * <p>Configuration is validated, not trusted. An id that is not a canonical mod id - one
 * containing spaces, slashes, or glob characters - is rejected and reported as a warning rather
 * than stored. That is what keeps a display name or a slur-shaped string out of the matching path,
 * and it is why canonical-id validation is never relaxed to accommodate one.
 */
public final class ModListDenylistConfig {

    /** Resource written on first run. */
    public static final String RESOURCE = "modlist-denylist.yml";

    private ModListDenylistConfig() {
    }

    /** Outcome of a load, including everything rejected and why. */
    public record Loaded(ModListEnforcement.Policy policy, List<String> warnings) {
        public ModListEnforcement enforcer() {
            return policy.enforcer();
        }
    }

    /**
     * Loads and validates the policy.
     *
     * <p>A malformed file yields the safe default - enabled but with an empty denylist - so a typo
     * cannot turn enforcement on with unintended entries, and cannot prevent the plugin starting.
     */
    public static Loaded load(Path dataFolder, Logger logger) {
        Path file = dataFolder.resolve(RESOURCE);
        if (!Files.isRegularFile(file)) {
            return new Loaded(ModListEnforcement.Policy.disabled(), List.of());
        }
        List<String> warnings = new ArrayList<>();
        try {
            YamlConfiguration yaml = YamlConfiguration.loadConfiguration(file.toFile());
            return new Loaded(read(yaml, warnings), warnings);
        } catch (RuntimeException malformed) {
            warnings.add("modlist-denylist.yml could not be parsed; using an empty denylist");
            logger.warning("modlist-denylist.yml could not be parsed; using an empty denylist: "
                    + malformed.getMessage());
            return new Loaded(emptyPolicy(), warnings);
        }
    }

    private static ModListEnforcement.Policy read(YamlConfiguration yaml, List<String> warnings) {
        boolean enabled = yaml.getBoolean("enabled", false);
        String configuredAction = yaml.getString("action", "KICK");
        ModListEnforcement.Mode mode = "AUDIT".equalsIgnoreCase(configuredAction)
                ? ModListEnforcement.Mode.AUDIT
                : ModListEnforcement.Mode.ENFORCE;

        String message = yaml.getString("message", "You were removed from the server.");

        Map<String, String> reasons = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        List<String> orderedIds = new ArrayList<>();

        // Canonical ids may be written either as a plain list of strings or as a mapping of
        // id -> reason. Both are exact; neither supports patterns.
        if (yaml.isList("denied-mod-ids")) {
            for (Object raw : yaml.getList("denied-mod-ids")) {
                addId(String.valueOf(raw), "", orderedIds, reasons, warnings);
            }
        }
        ConfigurationSection section = yaml.getConfigurationSection("denied-mods");
        if (section != null) {
            for (String rawId : section.getKeys(false)) {
                String reason = section.getString(rawId, "");
                addId(rawId, reason, orderedIds, reasons, warnings);
            }
        }
        if (!"KICK".equalsIgnoreCase(configuredAction) && !"AUDIT".equalsIgnoreCase(configuredAction)) {
            warnings.add("action '" + configuredAction + "' is not recognised; using KICK");
        }
        return new ModListEnforcement.Policy(enabled, mode, message, orderedIds, reasons);
    }

    /**
     * Validates and stores one configured id.
     *
     * <p>Rejects anything that is not a canonical mod id. A rejected entry is never matched against,
     * so a display name, a sentence, or a glob cannot become a denial rule.
     */
    private static void addId(String rawId, String reason, List<String> orderedIds,
                              Map<String, String> reasons, List<String> warnings) {
        if (rawId == null) return;
        String id = ModListDenylist.normalize(rawId);
        if (id.isEmpty()) return;
        if (!ModListDenylist.isCanonicalId(id)) {
            warnings.add("ignored non-canonical mod id '" + rawId
                    + "' (ids may contain only a-z, 0-9, '_', '-', and '.')");
            return;
        }
        orderedIds.add(id);
        reasons.put(id, reason == null ? "" : reason.trim());
    }

    private static ModListEnforcement.Policy emptyPolicy() {
        return new ModListEnforcement.Policy(false, ModListEnforcement.Mode.ENFORCE,
                "", List.of(), Map.of());
    }

    /** Renders the shipped resource text. Kept here so the file and the validator cannot drift. */
    public static String defaultResource() {
        return """
                # ==========================================================================
                # VAntiCheat - Forge mod-list denylist
                # ==========================================================================
                # Denies a connection when a Forge client declares an exact canonical mod
                # id from the list below.
                #
                # WHAT THIS IS EVIDENCE OF
                #   A Forge client sends its installed mod list to the server during the
                #   FML handshake. The ids in that list are a declaration by the client
                #   about its own installation. That is a far stronger signal than any
                #   heuristic, and matching is EXACT.
                #
                # WHAT IT IS NOT EVIDENCE OF
                #   This detects a mod that is PRESENT. It does not detect a cheat that is
                #   ACTIVE, and it says nothing about what a player did.
                #
                # IMPORTANT LIMITATIONS
                #   - Forge clients only. Fabric Loader transmits no mod list to a game
                #     server, so Fabric clients (including several well-known cheats)
                #     cannot be blocked this way at all.
                #   - Bedrock clients are excluded and are never probed.
                #   - Exact ids only. No substring, prefix, or display-name matching.
                #
                # The list ships EMPTY. Add ids deliberately, one per line, after verifying
                # each against a real client. An empty list denies nobody.
                # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

                # Master switch. When false, no connection is ever denied by this feature.
                enabled: false

                # KICK  - deny the connection on an exact match.
                # AUDIT - record the match in /vac status and allow the connection.
                action: KICK

                # Player-facing denial message. Deliberately does not name any mod or this
                # plugin: a message that reveals what triggered it tells someone how to
                # evade it.
                message: "You were removed from the server."

                # Canonical mod ids, written exactly as the client declares them.
                # These are placeholders showing the FORMAT. They are inert until an
                # operator replaces them with ids verified against a real client.
                #   denied-mod-ids:
                #     - your_mod_id_here
                denied-mod-ids: []

                # Equivalent form, when a reason should be recorded with each id.
                # denied-mods:
                #   some_mod_id: "reason recorded for administrators"
                denied-mods: {}
                """;
    }
}
```

`src/main/java/site/vackstudio/vanticheat/modlist/ModListEnforcement.java`:

```java
package site.vackstudio.vanticheat.modlist;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.Map;

/**
 * The single place a Forge mod-list observation becomes an allow / deny / audit decision.
 *
 * <p>Every rule the spec requires is concentrated here so it can be tested without a server, a
 * packet, or a player:
 *
 * <ol>
 *   <li>A denial requires a <b>complete and valid</b> mod list. Anything else - refused, truncated,
 *       wrong channel, wrong phase, absent - allows the connection. Garbage is never evidence.</li>
 *   <li>A denial requires an <b>exact canonical id</b> match. No substring, prefix, fuzzy, or
 *       display-name matching exists anywhere in this class.</li>
 *   <li>A denial requires enforcement to be <b>enabled</b>. In audit mode the same match is
 *       recorded and the connection is allowed.</li>
 * </ol>
 *
 * <p>The reason code is a constant, {@code FORGE_MOD_DENYLIST}, so an operator can distinguish a
 * denylist policy decision from an ordinary probe detection. It is deliberately not the string used
 * by the client-probe enforcement path, and it never reuses a probe result.
 */
public final class ModListEnforcement {

    /** Distinct, auditable reason. Never shared with client-probe enforcement. */
    public static final String REASON = "FORGE_MOD_DENYLIST";

    /** Configurable operator modes. */
    public enum Mode {
        /** Deny on an exact match. */
        ENFORCE,
        /** Record an exact match and allow the connection. */
        AUDIT
    }

    /** Configuration for this policy. */
    public record Policy(boolean enabled, Mode mode, String denialMessage,
                         List<String> deniedIds, java.util.Map<String, String> reasons) {

        /** A policy that denies nobody: the shipped default. */
        public static Policy disabled() {
            return new Policy(false, Mode.ENFORCE, "", List.of(), Map.of());
        }

        public ModListEnforcement enforcer() {
            return new ModListEnforcement(this);
        }
    }

    /** What the connection observer saw. */
    public enum ObservationStatus {
        /** A complete, valid mod list. Only this can support a denial. */
        COMPLETE,
        /** A payload arrived but was malformed or truncated. Never actionable. */
        MALFORMED,
        /** A handshake payload arrived that was not a mod list. Normal. */
        NOT_A_MOD_LIST,
        /** No Forge handshake was observed at all. Normal for vanilla, Fabric, and Bedrock. */
        UNSUPPORTED
    }

    /** One connection's observation. */
    public record Observation(ObservationStatus status, java.util.Map<String, String> mods,
                              ForgeModListParser.WireFormat format, String detail) {

        public static Observation complete(Map<String, String> mods,
                                           ForgeModListParser.WireFormat format) {
            return new Observation(ObservationStatus.COMPLETE,
                    java.util.Collections.unmodifiableMap(mods), format, "");
        }

        public static Observation malformed(String detail) {
            return new Observation(ObservationStatus.MALFORMED, Map.of(), null, detail);
        }

        public static Observation notAModList(String detail) {
            return new Observation(ObservationStatus.NOT_A_MOD_LIST, Map.of(), null, detail);
        }

        public static Observation unsupported(String detail) {
            return new Observation(ObservationStatus.UNSUPPORTED, Map.of(), null, detail);
        }
    }

    /** The decision. */
    public enum Outcome {
        /** Connection proceeds. */
        ALLOW,
        /** Connection is denied and must be disconnected. */
        DENY,
        /** An exact match was recorded under audit mode and the connection proceeds. */
        AUDIT
    }

    /**
     * A decision plus the evidence behind it.
     *
     * @param outcome what to do
     * @param reason  always {@link #REASON} when a match occurred, else a short diagnostic
     * @param matched the exact canonical id that matched, or null when none did
     */
    public record Decision(Outcome outcome, String reason, String matched, int modCount) {
        public boolean denied() {
            return outcome == Outcome.DENY;
        }
    }

    private final Policy policy;
    private final ModListDenylist denylist;

    /**
     * {@code deniedIds} is the sole authority for what is blocked.
     *
     * <p>{@code reasons} is metadata attached to those ids. Building the denylist from the reasons
     * map instead would let an id that was only ever given a reason become blockable, so the two are
     * kept strictly separate: ids decide, reasons annotate.
     */
    public ModListEnforcement(Policy policy) {
        this.policy = policy == null ? Policy.disabled() : policy;
        java.util.Map<String, String> annotated = new java.util.LinkedHashMap<>();
        java.util.List<String> ids = this.policy.deniedIds() == null
                ? List.of() : this.policy.deniedIds();
        for (String id : ids) {
            String normalized = ModListDenylist.normalize(id);
            if (normalized.isEmpty()) continue;
            String reason = "";
            if (this.policy.reasons() != null) {
                String configured = this.policy.reasons().get(id);
                if (configured == null) configured = this.policy.reasons().get(normalized);
                if (configured != null) reason = configured;
            }
            annotated.put(normalized, reason);
        }
        this.denylist = ModListDenylist.of(annotated);
    }

    public Policy policy() {
        return policy;
    }

    public ModListDenylist denylist() {
        return denylist;
    }

    /** Normalised ids actually configured. Shown by diagnostics. */
    public List<String> deniedIds() {
        return List.copyOf(denylist.blockedIds());
    }

    /**
     * Decides what happens to one connection.
     *
     * <p>Total and side-effect free: it reads configuration and an observation, and returns a
     * decision. It performs no I/O, touches no Bukkit state, and cannot throw for hostile input.
     */
    public Decision evaluate(Observation observation) {
        if (observation == null) {
            return new Decision(Outcome.ALLOW, "no observation", null, 0);
        }
        if (!policy.enabled()) {
            return new Decision(Outcome.ALLOW, "denylist disabled", null,
                    observation.mods() == null ? 0 : observation.mods().size());
        }
        // Rule 1: only a complete, valid list can support a denial. This is the single most
        // important guard in the class, because everything upstream can be fed by a hostile client.
        if (observation.status() != ObservationStatus.COMPLETE) {
            return new Decision(Outcome.ALLOW, "no complete mod list", null, 0);
        }
        if (denylist.size() == 0) {
            // An empty denylist denies nobody, by construction. The feature ships inert.
            return new Decision(Outcome.ALLOW, "denylist empty", null, observation.mods().size());
        }
        List<ModListDenylist.Match> matches = denylist.findMatches(observation.mods());
        if (matches.isEmpty()) {
            return new Decision(Outcome.ALLOW, "no denied id present", null, observation.mods().size());
        }
        String matched = matches.get(0).modId();
        int modCount = observation.mods().size();
        // Rule 3: mode decides whether a match is actionable.
        if (policy.mode() == Mode.AUDIT) {
            return new Decision(Outcome.AUDIT, REASON, matched, modCount);
        }
        return new Decision(Outcome.DENY, REASON, matched, modCount);
    }

    /** The configured player-facing message, or a neutral default. */
    public String denialMessage() {
        String configured = policy.denialMessage();
        return configured == null || configured.isBlank() ? "You were removed from the server."
                : configured;
    }

    /** Compact one-line diagnostic for {@code /vac status}. Never contains a raw payload. */
    public String describe() {
        return "modlist=enabled=" + policy.enabled()
                + " mode=" + policy.mode().name().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)
                + " denied=" + denylist.size();
    }
}
```

`src/main/java/site/vackstudio/vanticheat/modlist/PacketEventsBridge.java`:

```java
package site.vackstudio.vanticheat.modlist;

import java.lang.reflect.Constructor;
import java.lang.reflect.Method;
import java.util.UUID;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.logging.Level;
import java.util.logging.Logger;

/**
 * Owns the optional PacketEvents integration.
 *
 * <p><b>PacketEvents is an external plugin the operator installs.</b> Its API is a compile-time
 * dependency only; the interception runtime lives in the PacketEvents plugin, which owns the
 * server's Netty pipeline. VAntiCheat never shades or embeds it, because a second copy of the
 * pipeline hook in a shaded jar is how two libraries end up fighting over the same channel.
 *
 * <p>Everything here is therefore reflective. That is deliberate: the plugin must load and run with
 * the feature switched off and PacketEvents absent, so no class in this file may reference a
 * PacketEvents type in a signature that would fail to link.
 *
 * <p><b>Failure is explicit and inert.</b> If PacketEvents is missing, its API does not match, or
 * registration throws, the status becomes {@code UNAVAILABLE} with a reason, and the feature does
 * nothing at all. It never falls back to a second, less careful interception path.
 */
public final class PacketEventsBridge {

    /** Observable state of the integration. */
    public enum Status {
        /** Listener registered and active. */
        ACTIVE,
        /** PacketEvents is not installed, or the feature is switched off. */
        UNAVAILABLE,
        /** PacketEvents is present but the listener could not be registered. */
        FAILED
    }

    private final ModListConnectionRegistry registry;
    private final Logger logger;
    private volatile Status status = Status.UNAVAILABLE;
    private volatile String detail = "not initialised";
    private volatile List<Object> registeredListeners = List.of();

    public PacketEventsBridge(ModListConnectionRegistry registry, Logger logger) {
        this.registry = registry;
        this.logger = logger;
    }

    public Status status() {
        return status;
    }

    public String detail() {
        return detail;
    }

    public boolean active() {
        return status == Status.ACTIVE;
    }

    /**
     * Registers the Forge mod-list listener if, and only if, the feature is enabled and PacketEvents
     * is loaded.
     *
     * <p>Idempotent: a second call while active is a no-op, so a reload cannot double-register.
     *
     * @param enabled whether the operator enabled the feature
     * @return the resulting status
     */
    public Status initialise(boolean enabled, java.util.function.Consumer<UUID> denier) {
        return initialise(enabled, denier, null);
    }

    /** Registers the existing mod-list observer and optional terrain listener in one PE lifecycle. */
    public Status initialise(boolean enabled, java.util.function.Consumer<UUID> denier,
                             site.vackstudio.vanticheat.terrainmask.TerrainMaskService terrainMask) {
        if (!enabled) {
            status = Status.UNAVAILABLE;
            detail = "disabled by configuration";
            return status;
        }
        if (active()) {
            return status; // never register twice
        }
        try {
            Class<?> apiClass = Class.forName("com.github.retrooper.packetevents.PacketEvents");
            Object api = apiClass.getMethod("getAPI").invoke(null);
            if (api == null) {
                return unavailable("PacketEvents API not initialised");
            }
            Method eventManager = api.getClass().getMethod("getEventManager");
            eventManager.setAccessible(true);
            Object manager = eventManager.invoke(api);
            if (manager == null) {
                return unavailable("PacketEvents EventManager unavailable");
            }

            Class<?> commonListener = Class.forName(
                    "com.github.retrooper.packetevents.event.PacketListenerCommon");
            Method register = manager.getClass().getMethod("registerListener", commonListener);
            register.setAccessible(true);

            List<Object> listeners = new ArrayList<>();
            if (denier != null) listeners.add(newForgeListener(denier));
            if (terrainMask != null && terrainMask.isEnabled()) {
                Object terrainListener = newTerrainListener(terrainMask);
                if (!commonListener.isInstance(terrainListener)) {
                    throw new IllegalStateException("terrain listener is not a PacketEvents listener");
                }
                Method preflight = terrainListener.getClass().getMethod("preflight");
                Object preflightResult = preflight.invoke(terrainListener);
                Method listenerDetail = terrainListener.getClass().getMethod("detail");
                String runtimeDetail = String.valueOf(listenerDetail.invoke(terrainListener));
                if (!runtimeDetail.startsWith("READY")) {
                    terrainMask.integrationFailed(String.valueOf(preflightResult));
                    throw new IllegalStateException("terrain mask packet preflight failed: " + preflightResult);
                }
                if (!(terrainListener instanceof site.vackstudio.vanticheat.terrainmask.TerrainMaskPacketGateway gateway)) {
                    throw new IllegalStateException("terrain listener has no packet gateway");
                }
                terrainMask.installGateway(gateway, true, String.valueOf(preflightResult));
                listeners.add(terrainListener);
            }
            if (listeners.isEmpty()) {
                status = Status.UNAVAILABLE;
                detail = "no PacketEvents features are active";
                return status;
            }
            List<Object> registered = new ArrayList<>(listeners.size());
            for (Object listener : listeners) {
                registered.add(register.invoke(manager, listener));
            }
            registeredListeners = List.copyOf(registered);

            status = Status.ACTIVE;
            detail = "listeners registered=" + registered.size();
            logger.info("Forge mod-list enforcement=ACTIVE " + describe());
            return status;
        } catch (ClassNotFoundException absent) {
            if (terrainMask != null && terrainMask.isEnabled()) {
                terrainMask.integrationUnavailable("PacketEvents plugin is not installed");
            }
            return unavailable("PacketEvents plugin is not installed");
        } catch (ReflectiveOperationException | RuntimeException | LinkageError failure) {
            status = Status.FAILED;
            detail = failure.getClass().getSimpleName();
            if (terrainMask != null && terrainMask.isEnabled()) {
                terrainMask.integrationFailed(failure.getMessage());
            }
            logger.log(Level.WARNING, "Forge mod-list enforcement=FAILED reason=" + detail
                    + ". The feature is inert; VAntiCheat continues without it.");
            return status;
        }
    }

    private Object newTerrainListener(site.vackstudio.vanticheat.terrainmask.TerrainMaskService service)
            throws ReflectiveOperationException {
        Class<?> listenerClass = Class.forName(
                "site.vackstudio.vanticheat.platform.paper.TerrainMaskPacketListener");
        return listenerClass.getConstructor(site.vackstudio.vanticheat.terrainmask.TerrainMaskService.class,
                        Logger.class)
                .newInstance(service, logger);
    }

    private Status unavailable(String reason) {
        status = Status.UNAVAILABLE;
        detail = reason;
        logger.warning("Forge mod-list enforcement=UNAVAILABLE reason=" + reason
                + ". Install the PacketEvents plugin to enable it.");
        return status;
    }

    /**
     * Builds the listener reflectively.
     *
     * <p>Constructed through its PacketEvents superclass, because the concrete type cannot be named
     * here without linking PacketEvents into every code path.
     */
    private Object newForgeListener(java.util.function.Consumer<UUID> denier) throws ReflectiveOperationException {
        Class<?> listenerClass = Class.forName(
                "site.vackstudio.vanticheat.platform.paper.ForgeModListPacketListener");
        Class<?> peListener = Class.forName(
                "com.github.retrooper.packetevents.event.PacketListenerAbstract");
        // The listener must be registered as a PacketListenerCommon; verify before use.
        if (!peListener.isAssignableFrom(listenerClass)) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("listener is not a PacketEvents listener");
        }
        Constructor<?> constructor = listenerClass.getConstructors()[0];
        Object[] arguments = new Object[constructor.getParameterCount()];
        Class<?>[] types = constructor.getParameterTypes();
        for (int index = 0; index < types.length; index++) {
            if (types[index].isAssignableFrom(registry.getClass())) {
                arguments[index] = registry;
            } else if (types[index] == java.util.function.Consumer.class) {
                arguments[index] = denier;
            } else if (types[index] == Logger.class) {
                arguments[index] = logger;
            }
        }
        return constructor.newInstance(arguments);
    }

    /**
     * Unregisters the listener and releases all connection state exactly once.
     *
     * <p>Safe to call when never initialised, and safe to call repeatedly: the listener reference is
     * nulled before use, so a second call has nothing to unregister.
     *
     * <p>The registry is cleared here because this object owns it. Leaving tracked per-connection
     * entries behind after shutdown would be a memory leak on a server that reloads, and it would
     * let a stale decision outlive the listener that could have acted on it.
     */
    public void shutdown() {
        List<Object> listeners = registeredListeners;
        registeredListeners = List.of();
        int released = registry.clear();
        if (released > 0) {
            logger.fine("Forge mod-list state released entries=" + released);
        }
        if (listeners.isEmpty()) {
            status = Status.UNAVAILABLE;
            detail = "shut down";
            return;
        }
        try {
            Class<?> apiClass = Class.forName("com.github.retrooper.packetevents.PacketEvents");
            Object api = apiClass.getMethod("getAPI").invoke(null);
            if (api == null) return;
            Method eventManager = api.getClass().getMethod("getEventManager");
            eventManager.setAccessible(true);
            Object manager = eventManager.invoke(api);
            if (manager == null) return;
            Method unregister = manager.getClass().getMethod("unregisterListener", Class.forName(
                    "com.github.retrooper.packetevents.event.PacketListenerCommon"));
            unregister.setAccessible(true);
            for (Object listener : listeners) unregister.invoke(manager, listener);
        } catch (ReflectiveOperationException | RuntimeException | LinkageError failure) {
            // Shutdown must not throw. PacketEvents unloads with the server regardless.
            logger.log(Level.FINE, "PacketEvents listener unregistration failed reason="
                    + failure.getClass().getSimpleName());
        } finally {
            status = Status.UNAVAILABLE;
            detail = "shut down";
        }
    }

    /**
     * One-line diagnostic for {@code /vac status}. Contains no payload data.
     *
     * <p>Reports the count of tracked connections, not the denied ids themselves: an operator needs
     * to confirm the feature is live and bounded, not read the blocklist from a public status line.
     */
    public String describe() {
        return "forgeModList=" + status.name()
                + " trackedConnections=" + registry.tracked()
                + " detail=" + detail;
    }
}
```

`src/main/java/site/vackstudio/vanticheat/platform/AutomaticCheckCoordinator.java`:

```java
package site.vackstudio.vanticheat.platform;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Objects;
import java.util.UUID;
import java.util.function.BooleanSupplier;
import java.util.function.Consumer;
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentMap;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.LongAdder;
import java.util.logging.Logger;

/** Owns delayed automatic-check admission and per-player duplicate protection. */
public final class AutomaticCheckCoordinator {
    public record MetricsSnapshot(int active, int capacity, long admitted, long started,
                                  long released, long skippedAdmissions, long failures) { }

    private final Scheduler scheduler;
    private volatile long delayTicks;
    private volatile boolean firstJoinOnly;
    private volatile int maxConcurrent;
    private final Logger logger;
    private final ConcurrentMap<UUID, Pending> pending = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final Object admissionLock = new Object();
    private final LongAdder admittedCount = new LongAdder();
    private final LongAdder startedCount = new LongAdder();
    private final LongAdder releasedCount = new LongAdder();
    private final LongAdder skippedAdmissions = new LongAdder();
    private final LongAdder failures = new LongAdder();
    private volatile boolean stopped;

    public AutomaticCheckCoordinator(Scheduler scheduler, long delayTicks, boolean firstJoinOnly,
                                     int maxConcurrent, Logger logger) {
        this.scheduler = Objects.requireNonNull(scheduler, "scheduler");
        if (delayTicks < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("delayTicks cannot be negative");
        if (maxConcurrent < 1) throw new IllegalArgumentException("maxConcurrent must be positive");
        this.delayTicks = delayTicks;
        this.firstJoinOnly = firstJoinOnly;
        this.maxConcurrent = maxConcurrent;
        this.logger = Objects.requireNonNull(logger, "logger");
    }

    public boolean schedule(Target target, Runnable check) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(check, "check");
        return scheduleTicket(target, ignored -> check.run()) != null;
    }

    /** Returns an operation token so stale callbacks cannot complete a reconnect's scan. */
    public Ticket scheduleTicket(Target target, Consumer<Ticket> check) {
        return scheduleTicket(target, ignored -> { }, check);
    }

    /** Calls onAdmitted as soon as the UUID slot is reserved, before scheduling any work. */
    public Ticket scheduleTicket(Target target, Consumer<Ticket> onAdmitted, Consumer<Ticket> check) {
        return scheduleTicket(target, onAdmitted, check, ignored -> { });
    }

    public Ticket scheduleTicket(Target target, Consumer<Ticket> onAdmitted,
                                 Consumer<Ticket> check, Consumer<Ticket> onStartFailure) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(target, "target");
        Objects.requireNonNull(onAdmitted, "onAdmitted");
        Objects.requireNonNull(check, "check");
        Objects.requireNonNull(onStartFailure, "onStartFailure");
        Pending operation;
        Ticket ticket;
        long scheduledDelay;
        synchronized (admissionLock) {
            boolean online;
            try {
                online = target.online();
            } catch (RuntimeException exception) {
                failures.increment();
                logger.warning("Automatic client check admission failed for " + target.name()
                        + ": player state unavailable");
                return null;
            }
            if (stopped || !online || (firstJoinOnly && !target.firstJoin())) {
                skippedAdmissions.increment();
                return null;
            }
            if (pending.containsKey(target.id())) {
                skippedAdmissions.increment();
                return null;
            }
            if (pending.size() >= maxConcurrent) {
                skippedAdmissions.increment();
                logger.fine("Automatic client check skipped: concurrency limit reached for " + target.name());
                return null;
            }
            operation = new Pending(target.id());
            pending.put(target.id(), operation);
            ticket = new Ticket(this, operation);
            try {
                onAdmitted.accept(ticket);
            } catch (RuntimeException exception) {
                pending.remove(target.id(), operation);
                operation.completed = true;
                failures.increment();
                logger.warning("Automatic client check admission callback failed for " + target.name());
                return null;
            }
            if (operation.completed) return null;
            admittedCount.increment();
            scheduledDelay = delayTicks;
        }
        try {
            TaskHandle delayed = scheduler.runGlobalLater(() -> {
                if (!isCurrent(ticket)) return;
                try {
                    TaskHandle entity = scheduler.runAtEntity(new EntityTarget(target.nativeEntity()), () -> {
                        if (!begin(ticket)) return;
                        try {
                            if (!target.online()) {
                                fail(ticket, onStartFailure);
                                return;
                            }
                            check.accept(ticket);
                        } catch (RuntimeException exception) {
                            logger.warning("Automatic client check start failed for " + target.name()
                                    + ": " + exception.getMessage());
                            fail(ticket, onStartFailure);
                        }
                    }, () -> failBeforeStart(ticket, onStartFailure));
                    operation.entityHandle = entity;
                    if (operation.completed) cancel(entity);
                } catch (RuntimeException exception) {
                    logger.warning("Automatic client entity scheduling failed for " + target.name()
                            + ": " + exception.getMessage());
                    fail(ticket, onStartFailure);
                }
            }, scheduledDelay);
            operation.delayHandle = delayed;
            if (operation.completed) cancel(delayed);
            return ticket;
        } catch (RuntimeException exception) {
            complete(ticket);
            failures.increment();
            logger.warning("Automatic client check scheduling failed for " + target.name()
                    + ": " + exception.getMessage());
            return null;
        }
    }

    public boolean active(UUID playerId) {
        return pending.containsKey(playerId);
    }

    public int activeCount() {
        return pending.size();
    }

    public MetricsSnapshot metrics() {
        return new MetricsSnapshot(pending.size(), maxConcurrent, admittedCount.sum(),
                startedCount.sum(), releasedCount.sum(), skippedAdmissions.sum(), failures.sum());
    }

    /** Records join-policy skips that occur before coordinator slot admission. */
    public void recordSkippedAdmission() { skippedAdmissions.increment(); }

    public void reconfigure(long delayTicks, boolean firstJoinOnly, int maxConcurrent) {
        if (delayTicks < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("delayTicks cannot be negative");
        if (maxConcurrent < 1) throw new IllegalArgumentException("maxConcurrent must be positive");
        synchronized (admissionLock) {
            this.delayTicks = delayTicks;
            this.firstJoinOnly = firstJoinOnly;
            this.maxConcurrent = maxConcurrent;
        }
    }

    public void complete(UUID playerId) {
        Pending operation = pending.get(playerId);
        if (operation != null) complete(new Ticket(this, operation));
    }

    public boolean complete(Ticket ticket) {
        if (ticket == null || ticket.owner != this) return false;
        boolean removed;
        synchronized (admissionLock) {
            removed = pending.remove(ticket.operation.playerId, ticket.operation);
            if (removed) {
                ticket.operation.completed = true;
                releasedCount.increment();
            }
        }
        if (removed) cancelHandles(ticket.operation);
        return removed;
    }

    /** Claims the one final-result callback without releasing concurrency capacity yet. */
    public boolean claimCompletion(Ticket ticket) {
        if (ticket == null || ticket.owner != this) return false;
        synchronized (admissionLock) {
            return !ticket.operation.completed
                    && pending.get(ticket.operation.playerId) == ticket.operation
                    && ticket.operation.completionClaimed.compareAndSet(false, true);
        }
    }

    public boolean isCurrent(Ticket ticket) {
        return ticket != null && ticket.owner == this
                && !ticket.operation.completed
                && pending.get(ticket.operation.playerId) == ticket.operation;
    }

    public boolean isStarted(Ticket ticket) {
        return isCurrent(ticket) && ticket.operation.started;
    }

    private boolean begin(Ticket ticket) {
        synchronized (admissionLock) {
            if (ticket.operation.completed || ticket.operation.started
                    || pending.get(ticket.operation.playerId) != ticket.operation) return false;
            ticket.operation.started = true;
            startedCount.increment();
            return true;
        }
    }

    private void fail(Ticket ticket, Consumer<Ticket> onStartFailure) {
        if (complete(ticket)) {
            failures.increment();
            try {
                onStartFailure.accept(ticket);
            } catch (RuntimeException exception) {
                logger.warning("Automatic client check failure callback failed for "
                        + ticket.playerId() + ": " + exception.getClass().getSimpleName());
            }
        }
    }

    private void failBeforeStart(Ticket ticket, Consumer<Ticket> onStartFailure) {
        if (isCurrent(ticket) && !isStarted(ticket)) fail(ticket, onStartFailure);
    }

    public void disconnect(UUID playerId) {
        complete(playerId);
    }

    /** Cancels admission-delay work while leaving already-running sessions alone. */
    public void cancelNotStarted() {
        List<Pending> cancelled = new java.util.ArrayList<>();
        synchronized (admissionLock) {
            for (Pending operation : pending.values()) {
                if (!operation.started && pending.remove(operation.playerId, operation)) {
                    operation.completed = true;
                    releasedCount.increment();
                    skippedAdmissions.increment();
                    cancelled.add(operation);
                }
            }
        }
        cancelled.forEach(AutomaticCheckCoordinator::cancelHandles);
    }

    public void stop() {
        stopped = true;
        for (UUID playerId : List.copyOf(pending.keySet())) disconnect(playerId);
    }

    private static void cancelHandles(Pending operation) {
        TaskHandle delayed = operation.delayHandle;
        cancel(delayed);
        TaskHandle entity = operation.entityHandle;
        cancel(entity);
    }

    private static void cancel(TaskHandle handle) {
        if (handle == null) return;
        try {
            if (!handle.cancelled()) handle.cancel();
        } catch (RuntimeException ignored) {
            // Cancellation is best-effort; the operation token prevents stale work from running.
        }
    }

    public record Target(UUID id, String name, BooleanSupplier onlineState,
                         boolean firstJoin, Object nativeEntity) {
        public Target(UUID id, String name, boolean online, boolean firstJoin, Object nativeEntity) {
            this(id, name, () -> online, firstJoin, nativeEntity);
        }

        public Target {
            Objects.requireNonNull(id, "id");
            Objects.requireNonNull(name, "name");
            Objects.requireNonNull(onlineState, "onlineState");
            Objects.requireNonNull(nativeEntity, "nativeEntity");
        }

        public boolean online() { return onlineState.getAsBoolean(); }
    }

    public static final class Ticket {
        private final AutomaticCheckCoordinator owner;
        private final Pending operation;
        private Ticket(AutomaticCheckCoordinator owner, Pending operation) {
            this.owner = owner;
            this.operation = operation;
        }
        public UUID playerId() { return operation.playerId; }
    }

    private static final class Pending {
        private final UUID playerId;
        private volatile TaskHandle delayHandle;
        private volatile TaskHandle entityHandle;
        private volatile boolean completed;
        private volatile boolean started;
        private final java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicBoolean completionClaimed =
                new java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicBoolean();

        private Pending(UUID playerId) { this.playerId = playerId; }
    }
}
```
